definition: A structure built up of beams, columns, etc. with moment-resisting joints, such as gantry

name: Shelter
definition: A structure, fairly quick to setup, move or dismantle, used to give protection, especially from the weather or intrusion.

name: Signal Assembly
definition: An assembly to physically aggregate together one or more signal instances (and also sign instances) including any supporting structural elements such as a simple pole or a rigid frame gantry.

name: Slab Field
definition: Slabs, laid out in one plane.

name: Sump Buster
definition: An obstacle (with oil catchment basin) installed typically in a bus lane to prevent other traffic with lower ground clearance from using it. Also Sump breaker or Sump trap.

name: Supporting Assembly
definition: An assembly intends to support Overhead Contact Line [[System]]. It includes foundation, supporting elements and suspension assembly.

name: Suspension Assembly
definition: A complex assembly of components used to suspend elements or cable segments.

name: Track Panel
definition: Trackwork ensuring the support and guidance of a vehicle along a route. It consists of assembly of rail, sleepers and fastenings.

name: Traction Switching Assembly
definition: A common assembly used to insure the switching function. It is composed of switches, control instruments and other components.

name: Traffic Calming Device
definition: A structure on the carriageway to control the speed of vehicles.

name: Truss
definition: A structure built up of members with (quasi) pinned joint.

name: Turnout Panel
definition: Trackwork ensuring the support and guidance of a vehicle along any given route among various diverging or intersecting tracks.

name: Element Component
definition: An element component is a representation for minor items included in, added to or connecting to or between elements, which usually are not of interest from the overall building structure viewpoint. However, these small parts may have vital and load carrying functions within the construction. These items do not provide any actual space boundaries. Typical examples of _IfcElementComponent_s include different kinds of fasteners and various accessories.

name: Energy Conversion Device
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcEnergyConversionDevice]] defines the occurrence of a device used to perform energy conversion or heat transfer and typically participates in a flow distribution system. Its type is defined by IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType or its subtypes.

name: Engine
definition: An engine is a device that converts fuel into mechanical energy through combustion.

name: External Combustion
definition: Combustion is external.

name: Internal Combustion
definition: Combustion is internal.

name: Evaporative Cooler
definition: An evaporative cooler is a device that cools air by saturating it with water vapor.

name: Direct Evaporative Air Washer
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water dircectly into the air stream using coolers with spray-type air washer consist of a chamber or casing containing spray nozzles, and tank for collecting spray water, and an eliminator section for removing entrained drops of water from the air.

name: Direct Evaporative Packaged Rotary Air Cooler
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water dircectly into the air stream using coolers that wet and wash the evaporative pad by rotating it through a water bath.

name: Direct Evaporative Random Media Air Cooler
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water dircectly into the air stream using coolers with evaporative pads, usually of aspen wood or plastic fiber/foam.

name: Direct Evaporative Rigid Media Air Cooler
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water dircectly into the air stream using coolers with sheets of rigid, corrugated material as the wetted surface.

name: Direct Evaporative Slingers Packaged Air Cooler
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water dircectly into the air stream using coolers with a water slinger in an evaporative cooling section and a fan section.

name: Indirect Direct Combination
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water indirectly and without adding moisture into the air stream using a two-stage cooler with a first-stage indirect evaporative cooler and second-stage direct evaporative cooler.

name: Indirect Evaporative Cooling Tower or Coil Cooler
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water indirectly and without adding moisture into the air stream using a combination of a cooling tower or other evaporative water cooler with a water-to-air heat exchanger coil and water circulating pump.

name: Indirect Evaporative Package Air Cooler
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water indirectly and without adding moisture into the air stream. On one side of the heat exchanger, the secondary air stream is cooled by evaporation, while on the other side of heat exchanger, the primary air stream (conditioned air to be supplied to the room) is sensibly cooled by the heat exchanger surfaces.

name: Indirect Evaporative Wet Coil
definition: Cools the air stream by evaporating water indirectly and without adding moisture into the air stream. [[Water]] is sprayed directly on the tubes of the heat exchanger where latent cooling takes place and the vaporization of the water on the outside of the heat exchanger tubes allows the simultaneous heat and mass transfer which removes heat from the supply air on the tube side.

name: Evaporator
definition: An evaporator is a device in which a liquid refrigerent is vaporized and absorbs heat from the surrounding fluid.

name: Direct Expansion
definition: Direct-expansion evaporator.

name: Direct Expansion Brazed Plate
definition: Direct-expansion evaporator where a refrigerant evaporates inside plates brazed or welded together to make up an assembly of separate channels.

name: Direct Expansion Shell and Tube
definition: Direct-expansion evaporator where a refrigerant evaporates inside a series of baffles that channel the fluid throughout the shell side.

name: Direct Expansion Tube In Tube
definition: Direct-expansion evaporator where a refrigerant evaporates inside one or more pairs of coaxial tubes.

name: Flooded Shell and Tube
definition: Evaporator in which refrigerant evaporates outside tubes.

name: Shell and Coil
definition: Evaporator in which refrigerant evaporates inside a simple coiled tube immersed in the fluid to be cooled.

name: Event
definition: An [[IfcEvent]] is something that happens that triggers an action or response.

name: End Event
definition: A terminating event of a process.

name: Intermediate Event
definition: An event that occurs at an intermediate stage of a process.

name: Start Event
definition: An initiating event of a process.

name: External Spatial Element
definition: The external spatial element defines external regions at the building site.

name: External
definition: External air space around the building.

name: External Earth
definition: External volume covered by earth around the building.

name: External Fire
definition: Space occupied by a neighboring building.

name: External Water
definition: External volume covered with water around the building.

name: External Spatial Structure Element
definition: The external spatial structure element is an abstract entity provided for different kind of external spaces, regions, and volumes.

name: Facility
definition: A Facility (derived from [[IfcSpatialStructureElement]]) may be an [[IfcBuilding]], an [[IfcBridge]], an [[IfcRailway]], an [[IfcRoad]], an [[IfcMarineFacility]] (or any other type of built facility defined in the future, such as IfcTunnel).

name: Facility Part
definition: [[IfcFacilityPart]] provides for spatial breakdown of built facilities. It may be further specialised according to the type of facility being broken down.

name: Facility Part Common
definition: A part that is not clearly part of one domain but is a hybrid and has shared responsibilities in multiple domains.

name: Above Ground
definition: A vertical facility part for elements belonging to the space above the finished ground.

name: Below Ground
definition: A vertical facility part for the containment of elements below the finished ground. This may include for example earthworks elements and elements in a pavement structure.

name: Junction
definition: A longitudinal facility part providing an at grade junction between two or more segments of longitudinal facilities usually of the same type.

name: Level Crossing
definition: A longitudinal facility part providing an at grade crossing between two or more different modes of transport e.g. road and railway or road and pedestrian.

name: Segment
definition: A longitudinal facility part encompassing a linear portion of the facility defined by some uniform characteristics, or a transition between segments of uniform characteristics.

name: Sub Structure
definition: A vertical facility part comprising of an underlying or supporting structure. this can be above or below finished ground level.

name: Super Structure
definition: A vertical facility part comprising of the upper volume of a structure, usually forming the volume of operation or the receiving of live loading.

name: Terminal
definition: A longitudinal facility part that represents a termination segment of a longitudinal facility such as the end of a breakwater, road or rail section.

name: Fan
definition: A fan is a device which imparts mechanical work on a gas. A typical usage of a fan is to induce airflow in a building services air distribution system.

name: Centrifugal Air Foil
definition: Air flows through the impeller radially using blades that are airfoil shaped.

name: Centrifugal Backward Inclined Curved
definition: Air flows through the impeller radially using blades that are backward curved.

name: Centrifugal Forward Curved
definition: Air flows through the impeller radially using blades that are forward curved.

name: Centrifugal Radial
definition: Air flows through the impeller radially using blades that are uncurved or slightly forward curved.

name: Propellor Axial
definition: Air flows through the impeller axially and small hub-to-tip ratio impeller mounted in an orifice plate or inlet ring.

name: Tube Axial
definition: Air flows through the impeller axially with reduced tip clearance and operating at higher tip speeds.

name: Vane Axial
definition: Air flows through the impeller axially with guide vanes and reduced running blade tip clearance.

name: Fastener
definition: Representations of fixing parts which are used as fasteners to connect or join elements with other elements. Excluded are mechanical fasteners which are modeled by a separate entity ([[IfcMechanicalFastener]]).

name: Glue
definition: A fastening connection where glue is used to join together elements.

name: Mortar
definition: A composition of mineralic or other materials used to fill jointing gaps and possibly fulfilling a load carrying role.

name: Weld
definition: A weld seam between parts of metallic material or other suitable materials.

name: Feature Element
definition: A feature element is a generalization of all existence dependent elements which modify the shape and appearance of the associated master element. The [[IfcFeatureElement]] offers the ability to handle shape modifiers as semantic objects within the IFC object model.

name: Feature Element Addition
definition: A feature element addition is a specialization of the general feature element, that represents an existence dependent element which modifies the shape and appearance of the associated master element. The [[IfcFeatureElementAddition]] offers the ability to handle shape modifiers as semantic objects within the IFC object model that add to the shape of the master element.

name: Feature Element Subtraction
definition: The [[IfcFeatureElementSubtraction]] is specialization of the general feature element, that represents an existence dependent element which modifies the shape and appearance of the associated master element. The [[IfcFeatureElementSubtraction]] offers the ability to handle shape modifiers as semantic objects within the IFC object model that subtract from the shape of the master element.

name: Filter
definition: A filter is an apparatus used to remove particulate or gaseous matter from fluids and gases.

name: Air Particle Filter
definition: A filter used to remove particulates from air.

name: Compressed Air Filter
definition: A filter used to remove particulates from compressed air.

name: Odor Filter
definition: A filter used to remove odors from air.

name: Oil Filter
definition: A filter used to remove particulates from oil.

name: St Rain Er
definition: A filter used to remove particulates from a fluid.

name: Water Filter
definition: A filter used to remove particulates from water.

name: Fire Suppression Terminal
definition: A fire suppression terminal has the purpose of delivering a fluid (gas or liquid) that will suppress a fire.

name: Breeching Inlet
definition: Symmetrical pipe fitting that unites two or more inlets into a single pipe. A breeching inlet may be used on either a wet or dry riser. Used by fire services personnel for fast connection of fire appliance hose reels. May also be used for foam.

name: Fire Hydrant
definition: Device, fitted to a pipe, through which a temporary supply of water may be provided. May also be termed a stand pipe.

name: Fire Monitor
definition: Fire monitor.

name: Hose Reel
definition: A supporting framework on which a hose may be wound.

name: Sprinkler
definition: Device for sprinkling water from a pipe under pressure over an area.

name: Sprinkler Deflector
definition: Device attached to a sprinkler to deflect the water flow into a spread pattern to cover the required area.

name: Flow Controller
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowController]] defines the occurrence of elements of a distribution system that are used to regulate flow through a distribution system. Examples include dampers, valves, switches, and relays. Its type is defined by IfcFlowControllerType or subtypes.

name: Flow Fitting
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowFitting]] defines the occurrence of a junction or transition in a flow distribution system, such as an elbow or tee. Its type is defined by IfcFlowFittingType or its subtypes.

name: Flow Instrument
definition: A flow instrument reads and displays the value of a particular property of a system at a point, or displays the difference in the value of a property between two points.

name: AM Meter
definition: A device that reads and displays the current flow in a circuit.

name: Combined
definition: A device that reads and displays the value of multiple properties of a system at a point, or displays the difference in the value of a property between two points.

name: Frequency Meter
definition: A device that reads and displays the electrical frequency of an alternating current circuit.

name: Phaseangle Meter
definition: A device that reads and displays the phase angle of a phase in a polyphase electrical circuit.

name: Powerfactor Meter
definition: A device that reads and displays the power factor of an electrical circuit.

name: Pressure Gauge
definition: A device that reads and displays a pressure value at a point or the pressure difference between two points.

name: Thermo Meter
definition: A device that reads and displays a temperature value at a point.

name: Volt Meter
definition: A device that measures and displays the voltage in a circuit.

name: Volt Meter Peak
definition: A device that reads and displays the peak voltage in an electrical circuit.

name: Volt Meter Rms
definition: A device that reads and displays the RMS (mean) voltage in an electrical circuit.

name: Flow Meter
definition: A flow meter is a device that is used to measure the flow rate in a system.

name: Energy Meter
definition: An electric meter or energy meter is a device that measures the amount of electrical energy supplied to or produced by a residence, business or machine.

name: Gas Meter
definition: A device that measures the quantity of a gas or fuel.

name: Oil Meter
definition: A device that measures the quantity of oil.

name: Water Meter
definition: A device that measures the quantity of water.

name: Flow Moving Device
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowMovingDevice]] defines the occurrence of an apparatus used to distribute, circulate or perform conveyance of fluids, including liquids and gases (such as a pump or fan), and typically participates in a flow distribution system. Its type is defined by IfcFlowMovingDeviceType or its subtypes.

name: Flow Segment
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowSegment]] defines the occurrence of a segment of a flow distribution system.

name: Flow Storage Device
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowStorageDevice]] defines the occurrence of a device that participates in a distribution system and is used for temporary storage (such as a tank). Its type is defined by IfcFlowStorageDeviceType or its subtypes.

name: Flow Terminal
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowTerminal]] defines the occurrence of a permanently attached element that acts as a terminus or beginning of a distribution system (such as an air outlet, drain, water closet, or sink). A terminal is typically a point at which a system interfaces with an external environment. Its type is defined by IfcFlowTerminalType or its subtypes.

name: Flow Treatment Device
definition: The distribution flow element [[IfcFlowTreatmentDevice]] defines the occurrence of a device typically used to remove unwanted matter from a fluid, either liquid or gas, and typically participates in a flow distribution system. Its type is defined by IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType or its subtypes.

name: Footing
definition: A footing is a part of the foundation of a structure that spreads and transmits the load to the soil. A footing is also characterized as shallow foundation, where the loads are transferred to the ground near the surface.

name: Caisson Foundation
definition: A foundation construction type used in underwater construction.

name: Footing Beam
definition: Footing elements that are in bending and are supported clear of the ground. They will normally span between piers, piles or pile caps. They are distinguished from beams in the building superstructure since they will normally require a lower grade of finish. They are distinguished from STRIP_FOOTING since they are clear of the ground surface and hence require support to the lower face while the concrete is curing.

name: Pad Footing
definition: An element that transfers the load of a single column (possibly two) to the ground.

name: Pile Cap
definition: An element that transfers the load from a column or group of columns to a pier or pile or group of piers or piles.

name: Strip Footing
definition: A linear element that transfers loads into the ground from either a continuous element, such as a wall, or from a series of elements, such as columns.

name: Furnishing Element
definition: A furnishing element is a generalization of all furniture related objects. Furnishing objects are characterized as being

name: Furniture
definition: Furniture defines complete furnishings such as a table, desk, chair, or cabinet, which may or may not be permanently attached to a building structure.

name: Bed
definition: Furniture for sleeping.

name: Chair
definition: Furniture for seating a single person.

name: Desk
definition: Furniture with a countertop and optional drawers for a single person.

name: File Cabinet
definition: Furniture with sliding drawers for storing files.

name: Shelf
definition: Furniture for storing books or other items.

name: Sofa
definition: Furniture for seating multiple people.

name: Table
definition: Furniture with a countertop for multiple people.

name: Technical Cabinet
definition: A technical cabinet is a piece of furniture for holding, displaying and protecting technical appliances, usually organized in shelves, drawers or racks.

name: Geographic Element
definition: An [[IfcGeographicElement]] is a generalization of all elements within a geographical landscape. It includes occurrences of typical geographical elements, often referred to as features, such as trees or terrain. Common type information behind several occurrences of [[IfcGeographicElement]] is provided by the IfcGeographicElementType.

name: Soil Boring Point
definition: Soil boring point

name: Ter Rain
definition: Terrain

name: Vegetation
definition: Plant life or plant cover (as of an area). For example trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, ferns, and mosses.

name: Geomodel
definition: Representation of the concept of a volumetric geological and geotechnical model, usually an interpretation but sometimes created direct from ground penetrating measurement.; The assembly may contain one of more strata and other anthropic elements. The contained subtypes of [[IfcGeotechnicalStratum]] will have shape representations made from polyhedra or surfaces if a 'Yabuki' top surface model is being used.

name: Geoslice
definition: Representation of the concept of a sectional planar geological and geotechnical model, usually an interpretation but sometimes created direct from ground penetrating measurement. The assembly may contain one of more strata and anthropic elements. The contained subtypes of [[IfcGeotechnicalStratum]] will have shape representations made from polygons reflecting the visible section or poly lines if a 'Yabuki' top surface model is being used.

name: Geotechnical Assembly
definition: Representation of the abstract concept of a geological and geotechnical model, usually an interpretation but sometimes created direct from ground penetrating measurement.; Use of an assembly is optional but can carry the methodology and uncertainty information.; Such assemblies will include [[IfcGeotechnicalStratum]] entity types and may include other entity types such as [[IfcPile]], [[IfcSlab]] or [[IfcSensor]] to represent the capping, lining or logging equipment present.; [[IfcBorehole]] or [[IfcGeoslice]] can have a physical reality as a construction hazard alongside being the carrier for the interpreted results. Geological hazards may be associated to any [[IfcGeotechnicalAssembly]] or [[IfcGeotechnicalStratum]].

name: Geotechnical Element
definition: Abstract supertype for geotechnical entities.

name: Geotechnical Stratum
definition: Representation of the concept of an identified discrete almost homogeneous geological feature with either an irregular solid or 'Yabuki' top surface shape or a regular voxel cubic shape. A stratum is represented as a discrete entity, specialised (sub typed) from [[IfcElement]]. A stratum may be broken down into smaller entities if properties vary across the stratum or alternatively properties may be described with bounded numeric ranges. A stratum may carry information about the physical form and its interpretation as a Geological Item (GML).; The shape representations used should correspond to the sub-type of [[IfcGeotechnicalAssembly]] in which it occurs

name: Solid
definition: Representation of the concept of an identified discrete almost homogenous solid geological or surface feature, including discontinuities such as faults, fractures, boundaries and interfaces that are not explicitly modelled.

name: Void
definition: Representation of the concept of an identified discrete air filled geological feature, including caves and other voids.

name: Water
definition: Representation of the concept of an identified discrete water filled geological or surface feature including lakes, rivers and seas.

name: Grid
definition: [[IfcGrid]] ia a planar design grid defined in 3D space used as an aid in locating structural and design elements. The position of the grid (ObjectPlacement) is defined by a 3D coordinate system (and thereby the design grid can be used in plan, section or in any position relative to the world coordinate system). The position can be relative to the object placement of other products or grids. The XY plane of the 3D coordinate system is used to place the grid axes, which are 2D curves (for example, line, circle, arc, polyline).

name: Irregular
definition: An [[IfcGrid]] with u-axes, v-axes, and optionally w-axes that cannot be described by the patterns.

name: Radial
definition: An [[IfcGrid]] with straight u-axes and curved v-axes. All grid axes being part of V-axes have the same center point and are concentric circular arcs. All grid axes being part of u-axes intersect at the same center point and rotate counter clockwise.

name: Rectangular
definition: An [[IfcGrid]] with straight u-axes and straight v-axes being perpendicular to each other. All grid axes being part of u-axes can be described by one axis line and all other axes being 2D offsets from this axis line. The same applies to all grid axes being part of V-axes.

name: Triangular
definition: An [[IfcGrid]] with u-axes, v-axes, and w-axes all being co-linear axis lines with a 2D offset. The v-axes are at 60 degree rotated counter clockwise from the u-axes, and the w-axes are at 120 degree rotated counter clockwise from the u-axes.

name: Group
definition: [[IfcGroup]] is an generalization of any arbitrary group. A group is a logical collection of objects. It does not have its own position, nor can it hold its own shape representation. Therefore a group is an aggregation under some non-geometrical / topological grouping aspects.

name: Heat Exchanger
definition: A heat exchanger is a device used to provide heat transfer between non-mixing media such as plate and shell and tube heat exchangers.

name: Plate
definition: Plate heat exchanger.

name: Shell and Tube
definition: Shell and Tube heat exchanger.

name: Turnout Heating
definition: A device used to remove snow from railways. E.g. electric heating device, gas heater

name: Humidifier
definition: A humidifier is a device that adds moisture into the air.

name: Adiabatic Air Washer
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using an air washing element.

name: Adiabatic Atomizing
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using an atomizing element.

name: Adiabatic Compressed Air Nozzle
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using a compressed air nozzle.

name: Adiabatic Pan
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using a pan.

name: Adiabatic Rigid Media
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using a rigid media.

name: Adiabatic Ultrasonic
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using an ultrasonic element.

name: Adiabatic Wetted Element
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through adiabatic evaporation using a wetted element.

name: Assisted Butane
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through water heated evaporation using a butane heater.

name: Assisted Electric
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through water heated evaporation using an electric heater.

name: Assisted Natural Gas
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through water heated evaporation using a natural gas heater.

name: Assisted Propane
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through water heated evaporation using a propane heater.

name: Assisted Steam
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through water heated evaporation using a steam heater.

name: Steam Injection
definition: [[Water]] vapor is added into the airstream through direct steam injection.

name: Impact Protection Device
definition: An impact protection device is a component used to protect other built elements from kinetic damage.

name: Bumper
definition: A bumper is a buffer object at end of track that prevents driving over. It can be fixed on rails or the track panel, or can also be a natural element (e.g. rock, sand).

name: Crashcushion
definition: Technical note: Because this class is a 'Predefined Type' in IFC, meaning a specialisation of its par

name: Damping System
definition: An elastic element inserted between the superstructure (track and plate on slab track or ballast bed with ballast inserted in) and the tunnel structure (tunnel floor). Some of the elastic elements have a partial decoupling effect between the superstructure and underground due to vibrations. Both helical springs and elastomer blocks or elastomer strips can be used as suspension systems.

name: Fender
definition: A passive or active device formed of a damper and impact panel that is mounted on the quayside to protect against vessel impact.

name: Interceptor
definition: An interceptor is a device designed and installed in order to separate and retain deleterious, hazardous or undesirable matter while permitting normal sewage or liquids to discharge into a collection system by gravity.

name: Cyclonic
definition: Removes larger liquid drops or larger solid particles.

name: Grease
definition: Chamber, on the line of a drain or discharge pipe, that prevents grease passing into a drainage system.

name: Oil
definition: One or more chambers arranged to prevent the ingress of oil to a drain or sewer that retains the oil for later removal.

name: Petrol
definition: Two or more chambers with inlet and outlet pipes arranged to allow petrol/gasoline collected on the surface of water drained into them to evaporate through ventilating pipes.

name: Inventory
definition: An inventory is a list of items within an enterprise.

name: Asset Inventory
definition: A collection of asset instances of type [[IfcAsset]].

name: Furniture Inventory
definition: A collection of furniture instances of type [[IfcFurnishingElement]].

name: Space Inventory
definition: A collection of space instances of type [[IfcSpace]].

name: Junction Box
definition: A junction box is an enclosure within which cables are connected.

name: Data
definition: Contains cables, outlets, and/or switches for communications use.

name: Power
definition: Contains cables, outlets, and/or switches for electrical power.

name: Kerb
definition: A border of stone, concrete or other rigid material formed at the edge of the carriageway or footway.

name: Lamp
definition: A lamp is an artificial light source such as a light bulb or tube.

name: Compact Fluorescent
definition: A fluorescent lamp having a compact form factor produced by shaping the tube.

name: Fluorescent
definition: A typically tubular discharge lamp in which most of the light is emitted by one or several layers of phosphors excited by ultraviolet radiation from the discharge.

name: Halogen
definition: An incandescent lamp in which a tungsten filament is sealed into a compact transport envelope filled with an inert gas and a small amount of halogen such as iodine or bromine.

name: High Pressure Mercury
definition: A discharge lamp in which most of the light is emitted by exciting mercury at high pressure.

name: High Pressure Sodium
definition: A discharge lamp in which most of the light is emitted by exciting sodium at high pressure.

name: LED
definition: A solid state lamp that uses light-emitting diodes as the source of light.

name: Metalhalide
definition: A discharge lamp in which most of the light is emitted by exciting a metal halide.

name: OLED
definition: A solid state lamp that uses light-emitting diodes as the source of light whose emissive electroluminescent layer is composed of a film of organic compounds.

name: Tungsten Filament
definition: A lamp that emits light by passing an electrical current through a tungsten wire filament in a near vacuum.

name: Light Fixture
definition: A light fixture is a container that is designed for the purpose of housing one or more lamps and optionally devices that control, restrict or vary their emission.

name: Direction Source
definition: A light fixture that is considered to have a length or surface area from which it emits light in a direction. A light fixture containing one or more fluorescent lamps is an example of a direction source.

name: Point Source
definition: A light fixture that is considered to have negligible area and that emit light with approximately equal intensity in all directions. A light fixture containing a tungsten, halogen or similar bulb is an example of a point source.

name: Security Light Ing
definition: A light fixture having specific purpose of directing occupants in an emergency, such as an illuminated exit sign or emergency flood light.

name: Linear Element
definition: A generalization of all linear elements that are parts of an alignment.

name: Linear Positioning Element
definition: An [[IfcLinearPositioningElement]] is an entity describing positioning according to a curve.

name: Liquid Terminal
definition: A liquid terminal is a terminating or origination point for the transfer of liquid between distribution system(s). this is the point where the liquid distribution system interacts with the external environment. An example of this is a loading arm for the transfer of liquid from a docked vessel.

name: Hose Reel
definition: A Supporting framework on which a hose may be wound whose primary purpose is to connect and interact with the external environment.

name: Loading Arm
definition: A loading arm permits the transfer of liquid or liquefied gas from one system to another, through the use of an articulated arm that accounts for the movement of docked vessels.

name: Marine Facility
definition: A marine facility represents any major structure or entity that is specific to the ports and waterways domain. examples of this include quays, jetties, shipyards, breakwaters etc.

name: Barrier Beach
definition: a sand ridge that rises slightly above the surface of the sea and runs roughly parallel to the shore, from which it is separated by a lagoon.

name: Break Water
definition: A longitudinal structure that protects a shore area, harbour, basin or estuary from waves.;

name: Canal
definition: A man-made watercourse constructed usually, to join rivers, lakes or seas and often of a size suitable for navigation.;

name: Dry Dock
definition: a Dry dock is an enclosed chamber (by gate) that allows the draining of water for the construction or repair of marine vessels.;

name: Floatingdock
definition: A spatial element that encompasses a floating dry dock and supporting quay side ancillaries.

name: Hydrolift
definition: A type of vessel launch recovery facility, also known as a hydraulic lift dock, where ships are lifted vertically by water impounding systems, then floated laterally across the land to berths which subsequently become dry.

name: Jetty
definition: A berthing structure, that extends out into the sea usually perpendicular to the coastline, primarily for the transfer of liquid bulk materials.;

name: Launch Recovery
definition: Subset of facilities for the function of launching or recovering vessels.

name: Marine Defence
definition: A subset of facilities with the primary function of protection or defence of a coastal or flood area.

name: Navigational Channel
definition: A natural navigable watercourse (such as a river) that needs to be managed or have improvements applied. This includes defined navigational areas in open seas and bays.;

name: Port
definition: A complex/facility for shipping and marine activities, this includes cargo, people and storage of vessels (marinas harbours).

name: Quay
definition: a facility for the mooring of vessels accompanied with the loading and unloading of cargo or passengers or the maintenance of vessels.

name: Revetment
definition: A marine defensive structure made from earthworks, masonry or activities, built in such a way as to absorb the energy of incoming water.

name: Ship Lift
definition: A type of vessel launch recovery facility, where ships are lifted vertically out of the water on platforms connected to winches, then transferred horizontally to land based berths on rail, wheel or track systems.

name: Ship Lock
definition: A facility used for raising and lowering boats, ships and other watercraft between stretches of water of different levels on rivers and canal waterways or between impounded basins. This is achieved via an impounded chamber of water which is filled and emptied.

name: Ship Yard
definition: A coastal/waterside facility where ships are built and repaired.

name: Slipway
definition: A facility for the dynamic launch or recovery of a vessel utilizing an inclined ramp and gravitational or mechanical hauling systems.

name: Waterway
definition: A subset of facilities that have the primary function of providing a navigable area of water.

name: Waterway Ship Lift
definition: A facility used for raising and lowering boats, ships and other watercraft between stretches of water of different levels on river and canal waterways or between impounded basins. This is achieved via an impounded trough of water which is mechanically lifted up and down.

name: Marine Part
definition: Part of a marine facility.

name: Above Water Line
definition: A vertical spatial part that represents the part above the mean waterline defined within the site area.

name: Anchorage
definition: A region spatial part that represents a managed area for the anchorage of vessels awaiting space and conditions to enter a port.

name: Approach Channel
definition: A longitudinal spatial part of a waterway or port facility that covers the approach of the primary facility.

name: Below Water Line
definition: A vertical spatial part that represents the part below the mean waterline defined within the site area.

name: Berthing Structure
definition: A longitudinal spatial part of a waterway or port facility that provides facilities for the berthing of vessels while waiting for the waterway facility to become available. For example waiting for a lock cycle to complete and the lock gates to open.

name: Chamber
definition: A longitudinal spatial part of a waterway or port facility that forms the impounded chamber of a facility, such as a ship lock, dry dock or hydrolift

name: Cill Level
definition: A vertical spatial part that represents the elevation of the cill and floor level of an impounded facility such as a ship lock or dry lock.

name: Cope Level
definition: A vertical spatial part that represents the elevation working surface of the quay for the placement of quay furniture and plant.

name: Core
definition: A lateral spatial part that sub divides the core structure of a facility such as a breakwater or embankment

name: Crest
definition: A lateral spatial part that forms the crest area of breakwater or embankment where additional structures are placed such as access items or roads.

name: Gate Head
definition: A longitudinal spatial part of a waterway or port facility that forms the gate, supporting structure plant of an impounded facility such as a ship lock, dry dock or hydrolift.

name: Guding Structure
definition: A longitudinal spatial part of a waterway or port facility that forms the guiding and assistive structures at the entrance to an impounded facility.

name: High Water Line
definition: A vertical spatial part that represents the elevation of the high waterline, multiple high waterlines can be used to represent the different high tide types.

name: Land Field
definition: A region or lateral facility part that covers the land field of a waterside facility such as a quay.

name: Leeward Side
definition: A lateral spatial part that covers the side of protective structures that do not experience weather or wave effects.

name: Low Water Line
definition: A vertical spatial part that represents the elevation of the low waterline, multiple low waterlines can be used to represent the different low tide types.

name: Manufacturing
definition: A region spatial part that forms a sub division of a facility for the purpose of manufacturing. This covers areas that are open air and do not constitute a building or the building is only a small part of the entire area (in this case a child of type building can be used).

name: Navigational Area
definition: A region spatial part that covers a managed navigational area that is maintained for an operational reason, this could be a dredged turning circle or waiting area.

name: Protection
definition: A lateral or region spatial part that forms the area which contains protective measures for scour and erosion of a facility.

name: Ship Transfer
definition: A region spatial part that represents a clear area used for the transfer and movement of vessels this area could include complex rail tracks and additional loading requirements.

name: Storage Area
definition: A region spatial part that forms a sub division of a facility for the purpose of storing cargo. For example container stacks, dry bulk storage yards, material storage yards.

name: Vehicle Servicing
definition: A region spatial part that represents a functional division designed for the maintenance and/or storage of vehicles used for facility operations.

name: Water Field
definition: A region or lateral facility part that covers the water field of a waterside facility such as a quay.

name: Weather Side
definition: A lateral spatial part that covers the side of protective structures that is designed to protect and be impacted by weather or wave effects. such as the outer side of breakwaters or the riverside of flood embankments.

name: Material
definition: [[IfcMaterial]] is a homogeneous or inhomogeneous substance that can be used to form elements (physical products or their components).

name: Mechanical Fastener
definition: A mechanical fasteners connecting building elements or parts mechanically. A single instance of this class may represent one or many of actual mechanical fasteners, for example an array of bolts or a row of nails.

name: Anchorbolt
definition: A special bolt which is anchored into concrete, stone, or brickwork.

name: Bolt
definition: A threaded cylindrical rod that engages with a similarly threaded hole in a nut or any other part to form a fastener. The mechanical fastener often also includes one or more washers and one or more nuts.

name: Chain
definition: a series of linked metal rings used for fastening or securing something, or for pulling loads.

name: Coupler
definition: A part connecting two rod or bars, such as reinforcement bars.

name: Dowel
definition: A cylindrical rod that is driven into holes of the connected pieces.

name: Nail
definition: A thin pointed piece of metal that is hammered into materials as a fastener.

name: Nail Plate
definition: A piece of sheet metal with punched points that overlaps the connected pieces and is pressed into their material.

name: Rail Fastening
definition: An assembly of components which secures a rail to the supporting structure and retains it in the required position whilst permitting any necessary vertical, lateral and longitudinal movement.;definition from EN 13481-1.

name: Rail Joint
definition: A mechanical assembly with e.g. fishplates to join two rail ends with optional functions (insulation or expansion capacity).

name: Rivet
definition: A fastening part having a head at one end and the other end being hammered flat after being passed through holes in the pieces that are fastened together.

name: Rope
definition: a length of thick strong cord made by twisting together strands of hemp, sisal, nylon, or similar material. used primarily for mooring vessels

name: Screw
definition: A fastener with a tapered threaded shank and a slotted head.

name: Shear Connector
definition: A ring connector that is accepted by ring keyways in the connected pieces; or a toothed circular or square connector that is pressed into the connected pieces.

name: Staple
definition: A doubly pointed piece of metal that is hammered into materials as a fastener.

name: Stud Shear Connector
definition: Stud shear connectors are cylindrical fastening parts with a head on one side. On the other side they are welded on steel members for the use in composite steel and concrete structures.

name: Medical Device
definition: A medical device is attached to a medical piping system and operates upon medical gases to perform a specific function. Medical gases include medical air, medical vacuum, oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and nitrous oxide.

name: Air Station
definition: Device that provides purified medical air, composed of an air compressor and air treatment line.

name: Feed Air Unit
definition: Device that feeds air to an oxygen generator, composed of an air compressor, air treatment line, and an air receiver.

name: Oxygen Generator
definition: Device that generates oxygen from air.

name: Oxygen Plant
definition: Device that combines a feed air unit, oxygen generator, and backup oxygen cylinders.

name: Vacuum Station
definition: Device that provides suction, composed of a vacuum pump and bacterial filtration line.

name: Member
definition: An [[IfcMember]] is a structural member designed to carry loads between or beyond points of support. It is not required to be load bearing. The orientation of the member (being horizontal, vertical or sloped) is not relevant to its definition (in contrary to [[IfcBeam]] and [[IfcColumn]]). An [[IfcMember]] represents a linear structural element from an architectural or structural modeling point of view and shall be used if it cannot be expressed more specifically as either an [[IfcBeam]] or an [[IfcColumn]].

name: Arch Segment
definition: Individual segment of an arch structure.

name: Brace
definition: A linear element (usually sloped) often used for bracing of a girder or truss.

name: Chord
definition: Upper or lower longitudinal member of a truss, used horizontally or sloped.

name: Collar
definition: A linear element (usually used horizontally) within a roof structure to connect rafters and posts.

name: Member
definition: A linear element within a girder or truss with no further meaning.

name: Mullion
definition: A linear element within a curtain wall system to connect two (or more) panels.

name: Plate
definition: A linear continuous horizontal element in wall framing, such as a head piece or a sole plate.

name: Post
definition: A linear (usually vertical) member used to support something or to mark a point.

name: Purlin
definition: A linear element (usually used horizontally) within a roof structure to support rafters.

name: Rafter
definition: A linear elements used to support roof slabs or roof covering, usually used with slope.

name: Stay Cable
definition: A sloped element suspending a structure (such as bridge deck) from a pylon.

name: Stiffening Rib
definition: A linear element added to a flange or a web plate of a girder for local stiffening.

name: Stringer
definition: A linear element used to support stair or ramp flights, usually used with slope.

name: Structural Cable
definition: A linear cable element used to secure or stabilise a structure by resisting lateral and longitudinal loading through tension only, but cannot resist compression. usually formed of a flexible cable or wire.

name: Strut
definition: A linear element often used within a girder or truss.

name: Stud
definition: Vertical element in wall framing.

name: Suspender
definition: A vertical element suspending a structure (such as bridge deck) from a suspension cable or an arch.

name: Suspension Cable
definition: A suspended element, typically comprising steel wire, sheath, etc.

name: Tiebar
definition: A linear bar element used to secure or stabilise a structure by resisting lateral and longitudinal loading through tension and or compression. usually formed by a solid bar.

name: Mobile Telecommunications Appliance
definition: A mobile telecommunications appliance is a device that transmits, converts, amplifies or receives signals used in mobile networks.;This entity is used to define specific appliances used in mobile telecommunication networks. General communications appliances and those used in fixed transmission networks should be instantiated using [[IfcCommunicationsAppliance]].

name: Access Point
definition: An access point is a device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network.

name: Base Band Unit
definition: A baseband unit is a component of a distributed base transceiver station for implementing baseband processing functions.

name: Base Transceivers Tation
definition: A base transceiver station (BTS) is a network component which serves one cell. It completes the conversion between base station controller and wireless channel, and realizes the wireless transmission and related control functions between base station controller and mobile switching through the air interface.

name: E Utran Node B
definition: An E-utran nodel B is a logical network component which serves one or more E-utran cells. It is the hardware connected to the evolved packet core (EPC), more specifically to the mobility management entity (MME) , which communicates directly with user equipment in wireless way.

name: Gateway GPRS Support Node
definition: The gateway GPRS support node is a component of the GPRS core network that extends the GSM to allow packet switching functionalities. This component is responsible for the internetworking between the GPRS network and external packet switched networks (e.g. the internet).

name: Master Unit
definition: A master unit is a component of a repeater for coupling base station signals.

name: Mobile Switching Center
definition: The mobile switching centre (MSC) constitutes the interface between the radio system and the fixed networks. It is an exchange which performs all the switching and signalling functions for mobile station located in a geographical area designated as the MSC area. It consists of a MSC server and a media gateway.

name: MSC Server
definition: The MSC server mainly comprises the call control (CC) and mobility control parts of a mobile switching center (MSC). An MSC server and a media gateway make up the full functionality of an MSC.

name: Packet Control Unit
definition: A packet control unit performs some of the processing tasks of the base station controller for packet data. It is responsible for data packet, wireless channel management, error sending detection and automatic retransmission.

name: Remote Radio Unit
definition: A remote radio unit is a component of a distributed base transceiver station that converts digital baseband signals into high-frequency (rf) signals and sends high-frequency (rf) signals to the antenna for radiation.

name: Remote Unit
definition: A remote unit is a device used to amplify a base station signal.

name: Service GPRS Support Node
definition: The service GPRS support node (SGSN) is a component of the GPRS core network. It is the GPRS support node of mobile station service, and it can achieve mobility management and packet routing and transfer.

name: Subscriber Server
definition: It is a database in charge of the management of mobile subscribers. It can be an authentication center (AuC) or a home location register (HLR).

name: Mooring Device
definition: A mooring device is an active or passive built element who's primary function is to participate in the mooring of a vessel, this could be in the form of a bollard used as an attachment point for lines or active equipment such as quick release hooks.

name: Bollard
definition: a short, thick post on the deck of a ship or a quay side, to which ship's rope may be secured. not to be confused with traffic bollards.

name: Line Tensioner
definition: A mechanical device used to apply a tensioning load to mooring lines to improve vessel stability for port operations.

name: Magnetic Device
definition: Mooring device that uses magnets as the primary method of securing the vessel.

name: Mooring Hooks
definition: Quick release mooring hooks - an active device used to secure a vessel and provide automated release of vessels.

name: Vacuum Device
definition: Mooring device that uses vacuum suction as the primary method of securing the vessel.

name: Motor Connection
definition: A motor connection provides the means for connecting a motor as the driving device to the driven device.

name: Belt Drive
definition: An indirect connection made through the medium of a shaped, flexible continuous loop.

name: Coupling
definition: An indirect connection made through the medium of the viscosity of a fluid.

name: Direct Drive
definition: A direct, physical connection made between the motor and the driven device.

name: Navigation Element
definition: A navigation element is an active or passive built element who's primary function is to provide navigational instructions and warnings to vessels, this could be in the form of a floating buoy, a fixed beacon.; Navigation elements can aggregate other components and elements to form the entire structure. this might include a frame structure to form the body, instances of [[IfcSign]] for signage or instances of [[IfcSignal]] for supplementary lights an/or sound signals.

name: Beacon
definition: a fixed vertical structure serving as a navigation mark, to show reefs or other hazards, or provide navigational directions.

name: Buoy
definition: an anchored floating structure serving as a navigation mark, to show reefs or other hazards, or provide navigational directions.

name: Object
definition: An [[IfcObject]] is the generalization of any semantically treated thing or process. Objects are things as they appear - i.e. occurrences.

name: Object Definition
definition: An [[IfcObjectDefinition]] is the generalization of any semantically treated thing or process, either being a type or an occurrence. Object definitions can be named, using the inherited [[Name]] attribute, which should be a user recognizable label for the object occurrence. Further explanations to the object can be given using the inherited [[Description]] attribute. A context is a specific kind of object definition as it provides the project or library context in which object types and object occurrences are defined.

name: Occupant
definition: An occupant is a type of actor that defines the form of occupancy of a property.

name: Assignee
definition: Actor receiving the assignment of a property agreement from an assignor.

name: Assignor
definition: Actor assigning a property agreement to an assignor.

name: Lessee
definition: Actor receiving the lease of a property from a lessor.

name: Lessor
definition: Actor leasing a property to a lessee.

name: Letting Agent
definition: Actor participating in a property agreement on behalf of an owner, lessor or assignor.

name: Owner
definition: Actor that owns a property.

name: Tenant
definition: Actor renting the use of a property fro a period of time.

name: Opening Element
definition: The opening element stands for opening, recess or chase, all reflecting voids. It represents a void within any element that has physical manifestation. Openings can be inserted into walls, slabs, beams, columns, or other elements.

name: Open Ing
definition: An opening as subtraction feature that cuts through the element it voids. It thereby creates a hole. An opening in addition has a particular meaning for either providing a void for doors or windows, or an opening to permit flow of air and passing of light.

name: Recess
definition: An opening as subtraction feature that does not cut through the element it voids. It creates a niche or similar voiding pattern.

name: Outlet
definition: An outlet is a device installed at a point to receive one or more inserted plugs for electrical power or communications.

name: Audiovisual Outlet
definition: An outlet used for an audio or visual device.

name: Communications Outlet
definition: An outlet used for connecting communications equipment.

name: Data Outlet
definition: An outlet used for connecting data communications equipment.

name: Power Outlet
definition: An outlet used for connecting electrical devices requiring power.

name: Telephone Outlet
definition: An outlet used for connecting telephone communications equipment.

name: Pavement
definition: [[Type]] of built element in a road or other paved area to provide an even surface sustaining loads from vehicles or pedestrians, usually comprising several courses.;

name: Flexible
definition: Pavement with a bituminous surfacing and with a base layer with or without a hydrocarbon binder.

name: Rigid
definition: Pavement substantially constructed of cement concrete.

name: Performance History
definition: [[IfcPerformanceHistory]] is used to document the actual performance of an occurrence instance over time. It includes machine-measured data from building automation systems and human-specified data such as task and resource usage. The data may represent actual conditions, predictions, or simulations.

name: Permit
definition: A permit is a permission to perform work in places and on artifacts where regulatory, security or other access restrictions apply.

name: Access
definition: Enables access to an identified area.

name: Building
definition: Enables work to proceed by getting regulatory permissions.

name: Work
definition: Enables work to be carried out in an identified area.

name: Pile
definition: A pile is a slender timber, concrete, or steel structural element, driven, jetted, or otherwise embedded on end in the ground for the purpose of supporting a load. A pile is also characterized as deep foundation, where the loads are transferred to deeper subsurface layers.

name: Bored
definition: A bore pile.

name: Cohesion
definition: A cohesion pile.

name: Driven
definition: A rammed, vibrated, or otherwise driven pile.

name: Friction
definition: A friction pile.

name: Jetgrouting
definition: An injected pile-like construction.

name: Support
definition: A support pile.

name: Pipe Fitting
definition: A pipe fitting is a junction or transition in a piping flow distribution system used to connect pipe segments, resulting in changes in flow characteristics to the fluid such as direction or flow rate.

name: Bend
definition: A fitting with typically two ports used to change the direction of flow between connected elements.

name: Connector
definition: Connector fitting, typically used to join two ports together within a flow distribution system (e.g., a coupling used to join two pipe segments).

name: Entry
definition: Entry fitting, typically unconnected at one port and connected to a flow distribution system at the other (e.g., a breeching inlet).

name: Exit
definition: Exit fitting, typically unconnected at one port and connected to a flow distribution system at the other (e.g., a hose bibb).

name: Junction
definition: A fitting with typically more than two ports used to redistribute flow among the ports and/or to change the direction of flow between connected elements (e.g, tee, cross, wye, etc.).

name: Obstruction
definition: A fitting with typically two ports used to obstruct or restrict flow between the connected elements (e.g., screen, perforated plate, etc.).

name: Transition
definition: A fitting with typically two ports having different shapes or sizes. Can also be used to change the direction of flow between connected elements.

name: Pipe Segment
definition: A pipe segment is used to typically join two sections of a piping network.

name: Culvert
definition: A covered channel or large pipe that forms a watercourse below ground level, usually under a road or railway.

name: Flexible Segment
definition: A flexible segment is a continuous non-linear segment of pipe that can be deformed and change the direction of flow.

name: Gutter
definition: A gutter segment is a continuous open-channel segment of pipe.

name: Rigid Segment
definition: A rigid segment is continuous linear segment of pipe that cannot be deformed.

name: Spool
definition: A type of rigid segment that is typically shorter and used for providing connectivity within a piping network.

name: Plate
definition: An [[IfcPlate]] is a planar and often flat part with constant thickness. A plate may carry loads between or beyond points of support, or provide stiffening. The location of the plate (being horizontal, vertical or sloped) is not relevant to its definition.

name: Base Plate
definition: A plate used to spread load over a surface, such as underneath a bearing or column.

name: Cover Plate
definition: A plate (underneath or above) a flange to provide additional load capacity.

name: Curtain Panel
definition: A planar element within a curtain wall, often consisting of a frame with fixed glazing.

name: Flange Plate
definition: A flange plate in linear members having box or I-profile (e.g. top or bottom flange plate in box-girder).

name: Gusset Plate
definition: a plate or bracket for strengthening an angle in framework (as in a building or bridge).

name: Sheet
definition: A planar, flat and thin element, comes usually as metal sheet, and is often used as an additional part within an assembly.

name: Splice Plate
definition: A plate connecting two members joined at ends.

name: Stiffener Plate
definition: A transversal plate added to a flange or a web plate for local stiffening.

name: Web Plate
definition: A plate connecting flange plates in linear members having box or I-profile.

name: Port
definition: A port provides the means for an element to connect to other elements.

name: Positioning Element
definition: New and abstract entity definition for positioning and annotating elements that are used to position other elements relatively.

name: Procedure
definition: An [[IfcProcedure]] is a logical set of actions to be taken in response to an event or to cause an event to occur.

name: Advice Caution
definition: A caution that should be taken note of as a procedure or when carrying out a procedure.

name: Advice Note
definition: Additional information or advice that should be taken note of as a procedure or when carrying out a procedure.

name: Advice Warning
definition: A warning of potential danger that should be taken note of as a procedure or when carrying out a procedure.

name: Calibration
definition: A procedure undertaken to calibrate an artifact.

name: Diagnostic
definition: Diagnostic

name: Shutdown
definition: A procedure undertaken to shutdown the operation of an artifact.

name: Startup
definition: A procedure undertaken to start up the operation of an artifact.

name: Process
definition: [[IfcProcess]] is defined as one individual activity or event, that is ordered in time, that has sequence relationships with other processes, which transforms input in output, and may connect to other processes through input output relationships. An [[IfcProcess]] can be an activity (or task), or an event. It takes usually place in building construction with the intent of designing, costing, acquiring, constructing, or maintaining products or other and similar tasks or procedures..

name: Product
definition: The [[IfcProduct]] is an abstract representation of any object that relates to a geometric or spatial context. An [[IfcProduct]] occurs at a specific location in space if it has a geometric representation assigned. It can be placed relatively to other products, but ultimately relative to the project coordinate system. The ObjectPlacement attribute establishes the coordinate system in which all points and directions used by the geometric representation items under Representation are founded. The Representation is provided by an IfcProductDefinitionShape being either a geometric shape representation, or a topology representation (with or without underlying geometry of the topological items).

name: Project
definition: [[IfcProject]] establishes the context for information to be exchanged or shared, and it may represent a construction project but does not have to. The [[IfcProject]]'s main purpose in an exchange structure is to provide the root instance and the context for all other information items included.

name: Project Library
definition: An [[IfcProjectLibrary]] collects all library elements that are included within a referenced project data set.

name: Project Order
definition: A project order is a directive to purchase products and/or perform work, such as for construction or facilities management.

name: Change Order
definition: An instruction to make a change to a product or work being undertaken and a description of the work that is to be performed.

name: Maintenance Work Order
definition: An instruction to carry out maintenance work and a description of the work that is to be performed.

name: Move Order
definition: An instruction to move persons and artefacts and a description of the move locations, objects to be moved, etc.

name: Purchase Order
definition: An instruction to purchase goods and/or services and a description of the goods and/or services to be purchased that is to be performed.

name: Work Order
definition: A general instruction to carry out work and a description of the work to be done. Note the difference between a work order generally and a maintenance work order.

name: Projection Element
definition: The projection element is a specialization of the general feature element to represent projections applied to building elements. It represents a solid attached to any element that has physical manifestation.

name: Blister
definition: Part of concrete where the anchor for pre-stressing tendon can be embedded.

name: Deviator
definition: Part of concrete where re-direction of an external pre-stressed tendon can be embedded.

name: Protective Device
definition: A protective device breaks an electrical circuit when a stated electric current that passes through it is exceeded.

name: Anti Arcing Device
definition: An anti-arcing device is an equipment that prevents electric arc.

name: Circuit Breaker
definition: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal circuit conditions and also making, carrying for a specified time and breaking, current under specified abnormal circuit conditions such as those of short circuit.

name: Earthing Switch
definition: A safety device used to open or close a circuit when there is no current. Used to isolate a part of a circuit, a machine, a part of an overhead line or an underground line so that maintenance can be safely conducted.

name: Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker
definition: A device that opens, closes, or isolates a circuit and has short circuit protection but no overload protection. It attempts to break the circuit when there is a leakage of current from phase to earth, by measuring voltage on the earth conductor.

name: Fuse Disconnector
definition: A device that will electrically open the circuit after a period of prolonged, abnormal current flow.

name: Residualcurrent Circuit Breaker
definition: A device that opens, closes, or isolates a circuit and has short circuit and overload protection. It attempts to break the circuit when there is a difference in current between any two phases. May also be referred to as 'Ground Fault Interupter (GFI)' or 'Ground Fault Circuit Interuptor (GFCI)'

name: Residual Currents Witch
definition: A device that opens, closes or isolates a circuit and has no short circuit or overload protection. May also be identified as a 'ground fault switch'.

name: Spark Gap
definition: A spark gap is a device used to connect a circuit to earth in the event of a fault in live circuits.

name: Protective Device Tripping Unit
definition: A protective device tripping unit breaks an electrical circuit at a separate breaking unit when a stated electric current that passes through the unit is exceeded.

name: Electromagnetic
definition: A tripping unit activated by electromagnetic action.

name: Electronic
definition: A tripping unit activated by electronic action.

name: Residualcurrent
definition: A tripping unit activated by residual current detection.

name: Thermal
definition: A tripping unit activated by thermal action.

name: Varistor
definition: A high voltage surge protection device.

name: Voltage Limiter
definition: a voltage limiter is an equipment that prevents the over voltage.

name: Pump
definition: A pump is a device which imparts mechanical work on fluids or slurries to move them through a channel or pipeline. A typical use of a pump is to circulate chilled water or heating hot water in a building services distribution system.

name: Circulator
definition: A Circulator pump is a generic low-pressure, low-capacity pump. It may have a wet rotor and may be driven by a flexible-coupled motor.

name: Endsuction
definition: An End Suction pump, when mounted horizontally, has a single horizontal inlet on the impeller suction side and a vertical discharge. It may have a direct or close-coupled motor.

name: Splitcase
definition: A Split Case pump, when mounted horizontally, has an inlet and outlet on each side of the impeller. The impeller can be easily accessed by removing the front of the impeller casing. It may have a direct or close-coupled motor.

name: Submersible Pump
definition: A pump designed to be immersed in a fluid, typically a collection tank.

name: Sump Pump
definition: A pump designed to sit above a collection tank with a suction inlet extending into the tank.

name: Vertical Inline
definition: A Vertical Inline pump has the pump and motor close-coupled on the pump casing. The pump depends on the connected, horizontal piping for support, with the suction and discharge along the piping axis.

name: Vertical Turbine
definition: A Vertical Turbine pump has a motor mounted vertically on the pump casing for either; wet-pit sump mounting or dry-well mounting.

name: Rail
definition: A rail is a predominately linear built element that has a special section profile. Rail is distinctive from built elements with similar geometric shapes (e.g. beam, member) that its major function is to ensure guidance of moving for vehicles or other kinds of machineries.

name: Blade
definition: A blade is a machined rail, often of special section, but fixed and/or joined at the heel end to a rail to provide continuity of wheel support. The two switch rails in a set are the two inside rails. A switch rail is described as right or left hand according to whether it is part of a right hand or left hand half-set of switches.;definition from EN 13232-1-2004.

name: Check Rail
definition: A check rail is a rail laid close to the gauge face of a running rail which takes part in lateral guidance of the wheel and prevents derailment in small radius curved track and switches and crossings.;definition from EN 13481-1.

name: Guard Rail
definition: A guard rail is a rail that limits risk of train derailment, normally not loaded.

name: Rack Rail
definition: A rack rail is a building module for enhancing traction and break performance.

name: Rail
definition: A rail is a special section bar (usually of steel) ensuring the guidance of the wheel of a rolling stock or other heavy machineries. In railway, two rails are combined to form a track.

name: Stock Rail
definition: A stock rail is a fixed machined rail, ensuring the continuity on the main or diverging track with the switch in the open position. The machined part of the stock rail supports its switch rail in the closed position, giving continuity of line through this switch rail. The two stock rails in a set of switches are the two outside rails. A stock rail is described as right or left hand according to whether it is part of a right hand or left hand half-set of switches.;definition from EN 13232-1-2004.

name: Railing
definition: The railing is a frame assembly adjacent to human or vehicle circulation spaces and at some space boundaries where it is used in lieu of walls or to complement walls. Designed as an optional physical support, or to prevent injury or damage, either by falling or collision.

name: Balustrade
definition: Guardrail located at the edge of a floor, rather then a stair or ramp. Examples are balustrades at roof-tops or balconies, or along a bridge or on top of a retaining wall.

name: Fence
definition: Technical note: Because this class is a 'Predefined Type' in IFC, meaning a specialisation of its par

name: Guard Rail
definition: A type of railing designed to guard human or vehicle occupants from falling off a stair, ramp or landing where there is a vertical drop at the edge of such floors/landings, or to provide restraint to an errant road vehicle, installed on the central reserve of or alongside a road.

name: Hand Rail
definition: A type of railing designed to serve as an optional structural support for loads applied by human occupants (at hand height). Generally located adjacent to ramps and stairs. Generally floor or wall mounted.

name: Railway
definition: An [[IfcRailway]] is a spatial structure element as a route from one location to another for guided passage of wheeled vehicles on rails. An [[IfcRailway]] acts as a basic spatial structure element that supports to break down a railway project into manageable parts.;national or regional transport system for guided passage of wheeled vehicles on rails.

name: Railway Part
definition: Part of a railway.

name: Above Track
definition: A spatial structure element that contains elements that are positioned above or over the track, for example catenary lines and suspension systems.

name: Dilation Track
definition: Technical note: Because this class is a 'Predefined Type' in IFC, meaning a specialisation of its par

name: Line Side
definition: A spatial structure element that contains elements of the railway that are not in or over the tracks, hence line-side.

name: Line Side Part
definition: A spatial structure element to further divide a line-side part. It can be used to distinguish line-side parts into more manageable volumes, for engineering purposes.

name: Plaintrack
definition: A spatial structure element to further divide a track. It does do not contain any turnout panel or dilatation panel.

name: Sub Structure
definition: A spatial structure element that contains elements that are positioned below the track, for example the earthwork platform, prepared subgrade and embankment. This can be above or below finished ground level.

name: Track
definition: A spatial structure element that contains track-related elements, for example rails and sleepers.

name: Trackpart
definition: A spatial structure element to further divide a track,plain-track, turnout-track, dilatation-track.

name: Turnout Track
definition: A spatial structure element to further divide a track. It contains turnouts, and does not contain any plain track or dilatation panel.

name: Ramp
definition: A ramp is a vertical passageway which provides a human or vehicle circulation link between one floor level and another floor level at a different elevation. It may include a landing as an intermediate floor slab. A ramp normally does not include steps.

name: Ramp Flight
definition: A ramp comprises a single inclined segment, or several inclined segments that are connected by a horizontal segment, referred to as a landing. A ramp flight is the single inclined segment and part of the ramp construction. In case of single flight ramps, the ramp flight and the ramp are identical.

name: Spiral
definition: A ramp flight with a circular or elliptic walking line.

name: Straight
definition: A ramp flight with a straight walking line.

name: Half Turn Ramp
definition: A ramp making a 180° turn, consisting of two straight flights connected; by a halfspace landing. The orientation of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Quarter Turn Ramp
definition: A ramp making a 90° turn, consisting of two straight flights connected by; a quarterspace landing. The direction of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Spiral Ramp
definition: A ramp constructed around a circular or elliptical well without newels and; landings.

name: Straight Run Ramp
definition: A ramp - which is a sloping floor, walk, or roadway - connecting two levels.; The straight ramp consists of one straight flight without turns or winders.

name: Two Quarter Turn Ramp
definition: A ramp making a 180° turn, consisting of three straight flights connected; by two quarterspace landings. The direction of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Two Straight Run Ramp
definition: A straight ramp consisting of two straight flights without turns but with one; landing.

name: Referent
definition: [[IfcReferent]] defines a position at a particular offset along an alignment curve.

name: Boundary
definition: The referent represents where an administrative or maintenance boundary crosses the linear element being measured. This is typically the first time the boundary crosses the linear element. If the boundary runs along the linear element, it would be the point at which they first become collinear. The LRS (linear referencing system) should include specific rules about how boundaries are handled if this type of referent is permitted. If the linear element changes at the boundary as for a county route beginning at the county boundary, then the LRM (linear referencing method) is more correctly categorized as absolute.

name: Intersection
definition: The referent is the location of an intersection specified by the referent name. The intersection location is typically taken as the location of the intersection of the reference lines of the streets comprising the intersection and is, therefore, not necessarily precise or deterministic. Physical markers can be installed to remedy this. The LRS (linear referencing system) should include specific rules about how intersection locations are determined if this type of referent is permitted.

name: Kilo Point
definition: Kilo point

name: Landmark
definition: The referent is the location of a physical landmark visible in the field.

name: Mile Point
definition: Mile point

name: Position
definition: Used to fully describe a linearly referenced location given by the linear element being measured (the [[IfcAlignment]] into which the [[IfcReferent]] is nested), the method of measurement ([[Pset_LinearReferencingMethod]]) and a measure value ([[Pset_Stationing]]). If a linear referencing method is specified for the position, it overrides any linear referencing method specified for the alignment.

name: Reference Marker
definition: The reference marker is a notation referent, typically located in the right of way of the road, rail or other transportation system. Usually reference markers are initially spaced at a uniform distance along the linear element being measured, though subsequent re-alignments can result in uneven spacing between the markers.

name: Station
definition: [[Station]]

name: Super Elevation Event
definition: A kind of event that specifies the superelevation (cross slope) at a specific location along a road alignment, and the type of transition from the previous location. The locations are specified using an IfcLinearPlacement measured along the alignment axis curve.The element(s) that are affected by the superelevation event is currently proposed to be specified by containing the event in a specific lateral breakdown element of the road spatial structure (e.g. a Lane).

name: Width Event
definition: A kind of event that specifies the width at a specific location along a road alignment, and the type of transition from the previous location.
