The locations are specified using an IfcLinearPlacement measured along the alignment axis curve.; The element(s) that are affected by the width event is currently proposed to be specified by containing the event in a specific lateral breakdown element of the road spatial structure (e.g. a Lane or the entire carriageway).

name: Reinforced Soil
definition: Soil reinforced or stabilized by some mechanical or chemical method.

name: Dynamically Compacted
definition: The method of using dynamic tamping machine usually free falling a heavy hammer from the height, compacting the soil and quickly improving the bearing capacity of the foundation.

name: Grouted
definition: A method of injecting curable slurry into cracks or pores of a geotechnical foundation to improve its physical and mechanical properties.

name: Replaced
definition: Dig out the soft soil in a certain range below the foundation ground and then backfill the area with high strength, low compressibility and no corrosive materials.

name: Roller Compacted
definition: A kind of compacting method that adopts rolling machinery, repeated rolling and vibration compacts the foundation soil, increasing strength and descreasing compressibility.

name: Surcharge Preloaded
definition: A method that applies load to the foundation to discharge pore water, and the foundation is consolidated to improve the foundation strength. Unloading when the carrying capacity reaches the required level.

name: Vertically Drained
definition: A method to set vertical drainage measures in the foundation, so that pore water in the soil is discharged and the foundation strength is improved.

name: Reinforcement Definition Properties
definition: [[IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties]] defines the cross section properties of reinforcement included in reinforced concrete building elements. The property set definition may be used both in conjunction with insitu and precast structures.

name: Reinforcing Bar
definition: A reinforcing bar is usually made of steel with manufactured deformations in the surface, and used in concrete and masonry construction to provide additional strength. A single instance of this class may represent one or many of actual rebars, for example a row of rebars.

name: Anchoring
definition: Anchoring reinforcement.

name: Edge
definition: Edge reinforcement.

name: Ligature
definition: The reinforcing bar is a ligature (link, stirrup).

name: Main
definition: The reinforcing bar is a main bar.

name: Punching
definition: Punching reinforcement.

name: Ring
definition: Ring reinforcement.

name: Shear
definition: The reinforcing bar is a shear bar.

name: Space Bar
definition: A stirrup in pre-stressing system to position TendonConduit.

name: Stud
definition: The reinforcing bar is a stud.

name: Reinforcing Element
definition: A reinforcing element represents bars, wires, strands, meshes, tendons, and other components embedded in concrete in such a manner that the reinforcement and the concrete act together in resisting forces.

name: Reinforcing Mesh
definition: A reinforcing mesh is a series of longitudinal and transverse wires or bars of various gauges, arranged at right angles to each other and welded at all points of intersection; usually used for concrete slab reinforcement. It is also known as welded wire fabric. In scope are plane meshes as well as bent meshes.

name: Road
definition: A route built on land to allow travel from one location to another, including highways, streets, cycle and foot paths, but excluding railways. As a type of Facility, Road provides the basic element in the project structure hierarchy for the components of a road project (i.e. any undertaking such as design, construction or maintenance).

name: Road Part
definition: Part of a road.

name: Bicycle Crossing
definition: Designated level crossing over a road for cyclists.

name: Bus Stop
definition: Lateral part of Road for stopping buses allowing them to draw out of the traffic lanes and wait for short periods.

name: Carriageway
definition: Unitary lateral part of Road built for traffic. Carriageway may comprise several kinds of traffic lanes and lay-bys, as well as traffic islands, and in case of dual carriageway road they are separated by central reserve.

name: Central Island
definition: The center of a roundabout not intended for traffic, can be painted or upraised.

name: Central Reserve
definition: Lateral RoadPart separating two carriageways of the same road or separating traffic lanes and sidewalk.

name: Hard Shoulder
definition: A type of Shoulder that is surfaced, providing for safe use by vehicles in distress.

name: Intersection
definition: At-grade junction where two or more roads meet or cross. Intersections may be further classified by number of road segments, traffic controls, and/or lane design.

name: Layby
definition: A lateral part of Road where vehicles can divert from ordinary stream of traffic.

name: Parking Bay
definition: Lateral part of Road for parking vehicles.

name: Passing Bay
definition: A lateral part of Road that is a widening of an otherwise single lane road where a vehicle may move over to enable another vehicle to pass.

name: Pedestrian Crossing
definition: Designated level crossing over a road for pedestrians.

name: Railway Crossing
definition: At-grade crossing between road and railway.

name: Refuge Island
definition: A raised platform or a guarded area so sited in the carriageway as to divide the streams of traffic and to provide a safety area for pedestrians.

name: Road Segment
definition: Longitudinal, linear segment of a road, either defined by uniform characteristics, or as a transition segment (e.g. number of lanes changing).

name: Road Side
definition: A lateral RoadPart located along the Road adjoining the outer edges of the Shoulders. A general concept comprising the areas outside RoadwayPlateau not intended for vehicles.

name: Road Side Part
definition: A general concept for various parts of the Roadside.

name: Roadway Plateau
definition: Lateral part of Road comprising the carriageway(s), shoulders and medians.

name: Roundabout
definition: [[Type]] of at-grade junction at which traffic streams are directed around a circle.

name: Shoulder
definition: A lateral part of Road adjacent to, and usually at the same level as the Carriageway; not intended for vehicular traffic but may be used in case of emergency.

name: Side Walk
definition: A footpath along the side of a road. May accommodate moderate changes in grade (elevation) and is normally separated from the vehicular section by a kerb. There may be a central reserve or road verge between the sidewalk and traffic lanes.

name: Soft Shoulder
definition: A type of Shoulder that is not surfaced.

name: Toll Plaza
definition: A part of road facility where tolls are collected for use of toll road, tunnel or bridge.

name: Traffic Island
definition: A central or subsidiary area raised or marked on the carriageway, generally at a road junction or level crossing, shaped and placed so as to direct traffic movement and/or provide refuge for pedestrians.

name: Traffic Lane
definition: Lateral part of carriageway designated to vehicular traffic for a particular purpose.

name: Roof
definition: A roof is the covering of the top part of a building, it protects the building against the effects of weather.

name: Barrel Roof
definition: A roof or ceiling having a semicylindrical form.

name: Butterfly Roof
definition: A roof having two slopes, each descending inward from the eaves.

name: Dome Roof
definition: A hemispherical hip roof.

name: Flat Roof
definition: A roof having no slope, or one with only a slight pitch so as to drain; rainwater.

name: Freeform
definition: Free form roof.

name: Gable Roof
definition: A roof sloping downward in two parts from a central ridge, so as to form a; gable at each end.

name: Gambrel Roof
definition: A roof sloping downward in two parts from a central ridge, so as to form a; gable at each end.

name: Hipped Gable Roof
definition: A roof having a hipped end truncating a gable.

name: Hip Roof
definition: A roof having sloping ends and sides meeting at an inclined projecting; angle.

name: Mansard Roof
definition: A roof having on each side a steeper lower part and a shallower upper; part.

name: Pavilion Roof
definition: A pyramidal hip roof.

name: Rain Bow Roof
definition: A gable roof in the form of a broad Gothic arch, with gently sloping convex; surfaces.

name: Shed Roof
definition: A roof having a single slope.

name: Root
definition: [[IfcRoot]] is the most abstract and root class for all entity definitions that roots in the kernel or in subsequent layers of the IFC specification. It is therefore the common supertype of all IFC entities, beside those defined in an IFC resource schema. All entities that are subtypes of [[IfcRoot]] can be used independently, whereas resource schema entities, that are not subtypes of [[IfcRoot]], are not supposed to be independent entities.

name: Sanitary Terminal
definition: A sanitary terminal is a fixed appliance or terminal usually supplied with water and used for drinking, cleaning or foul water disposal or that is an item of equipment directly used with such an appliance or terminal.

name: Bath
definition: Sanitary appliance for immersion of the human body or parts of it.

name: Bidet
definition: Waste water appliance for washing the excretory organs while sitting astride the bowl.

name: Cistern
definition: A water storage unit attached to a sanitary terminal that is fitted with a device, operated automatically or by the user, that discharges water to cleanse a water closet (toilet) pan, urinal or slop hopper.

name: Sanitary Fountain
definition: A sanitary terminal that provides a low pressure jet of water for a specific purpose.

name: Shower
definition: Installation or waste water appliance that emits a spray of water to wash the human body.

name: Sink
definition: Waste water appliance for receiving, retaining or disposing of domestic, culinary, laboratory or industrial process liquids.

name: Toilet Pan
definition: Soil appliance for the disposal of excrement.

name: Urinal
definition: Soil appliance that receives urine and directs it to a waste outlet.

name: Washhand Basin
definition: Waste water appliance for washing the upper parts of the body.

name: Wc Seat
definition: Deprecated Hinged seat that fits on the top of a water closet (WC) pan.

name: Sensor
definition: A sensor is a device that measures a physical quantity and converts it into a signal which can be read by an observer or by an instrument.

name: CO2 Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects carbon dioxide.

name: Conductance Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects electrical conductance.

name: Contact Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects contact, such as for detecting if a door is closed.

name: Cosensor
definition: A device that senses or detects carbon monoxide.

name: Earthquake Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects the seismic wave and measures the seismic intensity in case of earthquake.

name: Fire Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects fire

name: Flow Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects flow in a fluid.

name: Foreign Object Detection Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects foreign objects that shock or break the power network. It may alarm when such accidents happen.

name: Frost Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects frost on a window.

name: Gas Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects gas concentration (other than CO2)

name: Heat Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects heat.

name: Humidity Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects humidity.

name: Identifier Sensor
definition: A device that reads a tag, such as for gaining access to a door or elevator

name: Ion Concentration Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects ion concentration, such as for water hardness.

name: Level Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects fill level, such as for a tank.

name: Light Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects light.

name: Moisture Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects moisture.

name: Movement Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects movement.

name: Obstacle Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects any obstacles.detectors sensing objects falling from a bridge, rock-fall detectors, etc.

name: Phsensor
definition: A device that senses or detects acidity.

name: Pressure Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects pressure.

name: Radiation Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects pressure.

name: Radioactivity Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects atomic decay.

name: Rain Sensor
definition: A device that senses or collects rainfall related information.

name: Smoke Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects smoke.

name: Snow Depth Sensor
definition: A device that senses or measures the depth of snowfall.

name: Sound Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects sound.

name: Temperature Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects temperature.

name: T Rain Sensor
definition: A device, usually attached to the rear end of the last vehicle of a train, acting on a fixed equipment to give an indication that the train is complete.

name: Turnout Closure Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects the position of a blade of a turnout.

name: Wheel Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects the passage of a wheel.

name: Wind Sensor
definition: A device that senses or detects airflow speed and direction.

name: Shading Device
definition: Shading devices are purpose built devices to protect from the sunlight, from natural light, or screening them from view. Shading devices can form part of the facade or can be mounted inside the building, they can be fixed or operable.

name: Awning
definition: A rooflike shelter of canvas or other material extending over a doorway, from the top of a window, over a deck, or similar, in order to provide protection, as from the sun.

name: Jalousie
definition: A blind with adjustable horizontal slats for admitting light and air while excluding direct sun and rain.

name: Shutter
definition: A mechanical device that limits the passage of light. Often used as a a solid or louvered movable cover for a window.

name: Sign
definition: A sign is a notice on display that gives information or instructions in a written, symbolic or other form. Signs are passive with the most common form of a pictorial panel. An instance of [[IfcSign]] refers to the occurrence of an individual panel which can be applied to a surface such as a wall or be aggregated within a Signal Assembly which can include multiple sign occurrences and the associated supporting structural elements (see Signal Assembly for examples).

name: Marker
definition: A Sign type formed of a vertical post (possibly with some lettering or symbols) usually used to delimitate distance or the location of some equipment.

name: Mirror
definition: A sign type that provides information via a reflective mirror surface.

name: Pictoral
definition: A sign type formed of a flat plate with some written or symbolic images on it.

name: Signal
definition: A signal is an active device that conveys information or instructions to users, by means of an audio, visual signal or a combination of both.; The primary distinction from an [[IfcSign]] is that a signal is active and therefore a subtype of [[IfcFlowTerminal]] usually requiring power and data connections for its operation.; An instance of [[IfcSignal]] represents a singular signalling device in a larger assembled unit or connected system, such as an individual frame within a railway signal, a single light unit in a traffic light system or an audio signal or light mounted on a navigational buoy.; Signals can be physically aggregated together into an assembly which can include multiple signal instances (and also sign instances) and the associated supporting structural elements such as a simple pole or a rigid frame gantry (see Signal Assembly for examples).; Signals can be logically (functionally) grouped together into a signalling system (a type of distribution system) to represent a connected group of signals for example a group of traffic lights controlling an road intersection.

name: Audio
definition: A signal type formed of an active device conveying information by emitting an audio signal such as a beep, ring, horn or explosive sound.

name: Mixed
definition: A signal type formed of an active device conveying information in both a visual and audio manner.

name: Visual
definition: A signal type formed of an active device conveying information in a visual manner such as a light, cluster of lights, or mechanical moving shapes.

name: Site
definition: A site is a defined area of land, possibly covered with water, on which the project construction is to be completed. A site may be used to erect, retrofit or turn down building(s), or for other construction related developments.

name: Slab
definition: A slab is a component of the construction that may enclose a space vertically. The slab may provide the lower support (floor) or upper construction (roof slab) in any space in a building.

name: Approach Slab
definition: Iis part of bridge abutment providing transition from embankment to the bridge

name: Baseslab
definition: The slab is used to represent a floor slab against the ground (and thereby being a part of the foundation). Another name is mat foundation.

name: Floor
definition: The slab is used to represent a floor slab or a bridge deck.

name: Landing
definition: The slab is used to represent a landing within a stair or ramp.

name: Paving
definition: Rigid pavement course of a road or other paved area, usually concrete.

name: Roof
definition: The slab is used to represent a roof slab (either flat or sloped).

name: Side Walk
definition: The slab is used to represent a sidewalk.

name: Tracks Lab
definition: A track slab is a reinforced concrete slab or prestressed reinforced concrete slab, which is a main element of slab track. It can be prefabricated or cast on site and may have sleepers embedded.

name: Wearing
definition: The slab is used to represent a wearing surface.

name: Solar Device
definition: A solar device converts solar radiation into other energy such as electric current or thermal energy.

name: Solar Collector
definition: A device that converts solar radiation into thermal energy (heating water, etc.).

name: Solar Panel
definition: A device that converts solar radiation into electric current.

name: Space
definition: A space represents an area or volume bounded actually or theoretically. Spaces are areas or volumes that provide for certain functions within a building.

name: Berth
definition: A space dedicated to the berthing of vessels within a port or managed area

name: External
definition: A space outside of a facility.

name: GFA
definition: Gross Floor [[Area]] - a specific kind of space for each building story that includes all net area and construction area (also the external envelop). Provision of such a specific space is often required by regulations.

name: Space Heater
definition: Space heaters utilize a combination of radiation and/or natural convection using a heating source such as electricity, steam or hot water to heat a limited space or area. Examples of space heaters include radiators, convectors, baseboard and finned-tube heaters.

name: Convector
definition: A heat-distributing unit that operates with gravity-circulated air.

name: Radiator
definition: A heat-distributing unit that operates with thermal radiation.

name: Internal
definition: A space inside a facility.

name: Parking
definition: A space dedication for use as a parking spot for vehicles, including access, such as a parking aisle.

name: Space
definition: Any space not falling into another category.

name: Spatial Element
definition: A spatial element is the generalization of all spatial elements that might be used to define a spatial structure or to define spatial zones.

name: Spatial Structure Element
definition: A spatial structure element is the generalization of all spatial elements that might be used to define a spatial structure. The spatial structure can be used to provide a spatial organization of a project.

name: Spatial Zone
definition: A spatial zone is a non-hierarchical and potentially overlapping decomposition of the project under some functional consideration. A spatial zone might be used to represent a thermal zone, a construction zone, a lighting zone, a usable area zone. A spatial zone might have its independent placement and shape representation.

name: Construction
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a construction zone for the production process.

name: Fire Safety
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a fire safety zone, or fire compartment.

name: Interference
definition: The spatial zone is used to define an interference between [[IfcSpatialElement]] occurrences.

name: Light Ing
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a lighting zone; a daylight zone, or an artificial lighting zone.

name: Occupancy
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a zone of particular occupancy.

name: Reservation
definition: A spatial zone that marks some sort of reservation within the project extent.

name: Security
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a zone for security planning and maintenance work.

name: Thermal
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a thermal zone.

name: Transport
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent an area primarily dedicated to the movement of people or goods.

name: Ventilation
definition: The spatial zone is used to represent a ventilation zone.

name: Stack Terminal
definition: A stack terminal is placed at the top of a ventilating stack (such as to prevent ingress by birds or rainwater) or rainwater pipe (to act as a collector or hopper for discharge from guttering).

name: Bird Cage
definition: Guard cage, typically wire mesh, at the top of the stack preventing access by birds.

name: Cowl
definition: A cowling placed at the top of a stack to eliminate downdraft.

name: Rain Water Hopper
definition: A box placed at the top of a rainwater downpipe to catch rainwater from guttering.

name: Stair
definition: A stair is a vertical passageway allowing occupants to walk (step) from one floor level to another floor level at a different elevation. It may include a landing as an intermediate floor slab.

name: Curved Run Stair
definition: A stair extending from one level to another without turns or winders. The stair is consisting of one curved flight.

name: Double Return Stair
definition: A stair having one straight flight to a wide quarterspace landing, and two side flights from that landing into opposite directions. The stair is making a 90° turn. The direction of traffic is determined by the walking line.

name: Stair Flight
definition: A stair flight is an assembly of building components in a single 'run' of stair steps (not interrupted by a landing). The stair steps and any stringers are included in the stair flight. A winder is also regarded a part of a stair flight.

name: Curved
definition: A stair flight with a curved walking line.

name: Freeform
definition: A stair flight with a free form walking line (and outer boundaries).

name: Spiral
definition: A stair flight with a circular or elliptic walking line.

name: Straight
definition: A stair flight with a straight walking line.

name: Winder
definition: A stair flight with a walking line including straight and curved sections.

name: Half Turn Stair
definition: A stair making a 180° turn, consisting of two straight flights connectedby a halfspace landing. The orientation of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Half Wind Ing Stair
definition: A stair consisting of one flight with one half winder, which makes a 180° turn. The orientation of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Ladder
definition: a piece of equipment consisting of a series of bars or steps between two upright elements used for climbing up or down something

name: Quarter Turn Stair
definition: A stair making a 90° turn, consisting of two straight flights connected by a quarterspace landing. The direction of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Quarter Wind Ing Stair
definition: A stair consisting of one flight with a quarter winder, which is making a 90° turn. The direction of the turn is determined by the walking line.

name: Spiral Stair
definition: A stair constructed with winders around a circular newel often without landings. Depending on outer boundary it can be either a circular, elliptical or rectangular spiral stair. The orientation of the winding stairs is determined by the walking line.

name: Straight Run Stair
definition: A stair extending from one level to another without turns or winders. The stair consists of one straight flight.

name: Three Quarter Turn Stair
definition: A stair making a 270° turn, consisting of four straight flights connected; by three quarterspace landings. The direction of the turns is determined by the walking line.

name: Three Quarter Wind Ing Stair
definition: A stair consisting of one flight with three quarter winders, which make a; 90° turn. The stair makes a 270° turn. The direction of the turns is determined by the walking line.

name: Two Curved Run Stair
definition: A curved stair consisting of two curved flights without turns but with one landing.

name: Two Quarter Turn Stair
definition: A stair making a 180° turn, consisting of three straight flights connected by two quarterspace landings. The direction of the turns is determined by the walking line.

name: Two Quarter Wind Ing Stair
definition: A stair consisting of one flight with two quarter winders, which make a; 90° turn. The stair makes a 180° turn. The direction of the turns is determined by the walking line.

name: Two Straight Run Stair
definition: A straight stair consisting of two straight flights without turns but with one landing.

name: Structural Action
definition: A structural action is a structural activity that acts upon a structural item or building element.

name: Structural Activity
definition: The abstract entity [[IfcStructuralActivity]] combines the definition of actions (such as forces, displacements, etc.) and reactions (support reactions, internal forces, deflections, etc.) which are specified by using the basic load definitions from the IfcStructuralLoadResource.

name: Structural Analysis Model
definition: The [[IfcStructuralAnalysisModel]] is used to assemble all information needed to represent a structural analysis model. It encompasses certain general properties (such as analysis type), references to all contained structural members, structural supports or connections, as well as loads and the respective load results.

name: In Plane Loading 2D
definition: In plan loading 2D

name: Loading 3D
definition: Loading 3D

name: Out Plane Loading 2D
definition: Out plane loading 2D

name: Structural Connection
definition: An [[IfcStructuralConnection]] represents a structural connection object (node connection, edge connection, or surface connection) or supports.

name: Structural Curve Action
definition: A structural curve action defines an action which is distributed over a curve. A curve action may be connected with a curve member or curve connection, or surface member or surface connection.

name: Const
definition: The load has a constant value over its entire extent.

name: Discrete
definition: The load is specified as a series of discrete load points.

name: Equidistant
definition: The load consists of n consecutive sections of same length and is specified by n+1 load samples. The interpolation type over the segments is not defined by this distribution type but may be qualified in [[IfcObject]].[[ObjectType]] based on additional agreements.

name: Linear
definition: The load value is linearly distributed over the load's extent.

name: Parabola
definition: The load value is distributed as a half wave described by a symmetric quadratic parabola.

name: Polygonal
definition: The load consists of several consecutive linear sections.

name: Sinus
definition: The load value is distributed as a sinus half wave.

name: Structural Curve Connection
definition: Instances of [[IfcStructuralCurveConnection]] describe edge 'nodes', i.e. edges where two or more surface members are joined, or edge supports. Edge curves may be straight or curved.

name: Structural Curve Member
definition: Instances of [[IfcStructuralCurveMember]] describe edge members, i.e. structural analysis idealizations of beams, columns, rods etc. Curve members may be straight or curved.

name: Cable
definition: A tension member which is able to carry transverse loads only under large deflection.

name: Compression Member
definition: A member without tensional stiffness.

name: Pin Joined Member
definition: A member with capacity to carry axial loads only, i.e. a link. Typically used in trusses.

name: Rigid Joined Member
definition: A member with capacity to carry transverse and axial loads, i.e. a beam. Its actual joints may be rigid or pinned. Typically used in rigid frames.

name: Tension Member
definition: A member without compressional stiffness.

name: Structural Curve Member Varying
definition: This entity describes edge members with varying profile properties. Each instance of [[IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying]] is composed of two or more instances of [[IfcStructuralCurveMember]] with differing profile properties. These subordinate members relate to the instance of [[IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying]] by IfcRelAggregates.

name: Structural Curve Reaction
definition: This entity defines a reaction which occurs distributed over a curve. A curve reaction may be connected with a curve member or curve connection, or surface member or surface connection.

name: Const
definition: The load has a constant value over its entire extent.

name: Discrete
definition: The load is specified as a series of discrete load points.

name: Equidistant
definition: The load consists of n consecutive sections of same length and is specified by n+1 load samples. The interpolation type over the segments is not defined by this distribution type but may be qualified in [[IfcObject]].[[ObjectType]] based on additional agreements.

name: Linear
definition: The load value is linearly distributed over the load's extent.

name: Parabola
definition: The load value is distributed as a half wave described by a symmetric quadratic parabola.

name: Polygonal
definition: The load consists of several consecutive linear sections.

name: Sinus
definition: The load value is distributed as a sinus half wave.

name: Structural Item
definition: The abstract entity [[IfcStructuralItem]] is the generalization of structural members and structural connections, that is, analysis idealizations of elements in the building model. It defines the relation between structural members and connections with structural activities (actions and reactions).

name: Structural Linear Action
definition: This entity defines an action with constant value which is distributed over a curve.

name: Structural Load
definition: This abstract entity is the supertype of all loads (actions or reactions) or of certain requirements resulting from structural analysis, or certain provisions which influence structural analysis.

name: Structural Load Case
definition: A load case is a load group, commonly used to group loads from the same action source.

name: Structural Load Group
definition: The entity [[IfcStructuralLoadGroup]] is used to structure the physical impacts. By using the grouping features inherited from [[IfcGroup]], instances of [[IfcStructuralAction]] (or its subclasses) and of [[IfcStructuralLoadGroup]] can be used to define load groups, load cases and load combinations. (See also IfcLoadGroupTypeEnum.)

name: Load Case
definition: Groups LOAD_GROUPs and instances of subtypes of [[IfcStructuralAction]].; It should be used as a container for loads with the same origin.

name: Load Combination
definition: An intermediate level between LOAD_CASE and LOAD_COMBINATION. This level is obsolete and deprecated. Before the introduction of IfcRelAssignsToGroupByFactor, the purpose of this level was to provide a factor with which one or more LOAD_CASEs occur in a LOAD_COMBINATION.

name: Load Group
definition: Groups instances of subtypes of [[IfcStructuralAction]]. It shall be used as a container for loads grouped together for specific purposes, such as loads which are part of a special load pattern.

name: Structural Member
definition: The abstract entity [[IfcStructuralMember]] is the superclass of all structural items which represent the idealized structural behavior of building elements.

name: Structural Planar Action
definition: This entity defines an action with constant value which is distributed over a surface.

name: Structural Point Action
definition: This entity defines an action which acts on a point. A point action is typically connected with a point connection. It may also be connected with a curve member or curve connection, or surface member or surface connection.

name: Structural Point Connection
definition: Instances of [[IfcStructuralPointConnection]] describe structural nodes or point supports.

name: Structural Point Reaction
definition: This entity defines a reaction which occurs at a point. A point reaction is typically connected with a point connection. It may also be connected with a curve member or curve connection, or surface member or surface connection.

name: Structural Reaction
definition: A structural reaction is a structural activity that results from a structural action imposed to a structural item or building element. Examples are support reactions, internal forces, and deflections.

name: Structural Result Group
definition: Instances of the entity [[IfcStructuralResultGroup]] are used to group results of structural analysis calculations and to capture the connection to the underlying basic load group. The basic functionality for grouping inherited from [[IfcGroup]] is used to collect instances from [[IfcStructuralReaction]] or its respective subclasses.

name: Structural Surface Action
definition: This entity defines an action which is distributed over a surface. A surface action may be connected with a surface member or surface connection.

name: Bilinear
definition: The load value is bilinearly distributed over the load's extent.

name: Const
definition: The load has a constant value over its entire extent.

name: Discrete
definition: The load is specified as a series of discrete load points.

name: Isocontour
definition: The load is specified by a series of iso-curves (level sets), i.e. curves at which the load value is constant. These curves run perpendicularly to the load gradient.

name: Structural Surface Connection
definition: Instances of [[IfcStructuralSurfaceConnection]] describe face 'nodes', i.e. faces where two or more surface members are joined, or face supports. Face surfaces may be planar or curved.

name: Structural Surface Member
definition: Instances of [[IfcStructuralSurfaceMember]] describe face members, that is, structural analysis idealizations of slabs, walls, and shells. Surface members may be planar or curved.

name: Bending Element
definition: A member with capacity to carry out-of-plane loads, i.e. a plate.

name: Membrane Element
definition: A member with capacity to carry in-plane loads, for example a shear wall.

name: Shell
definition: A member with capacity to carry in-plane and out-of-plane loads, i.e. a combination of bending element and membrane element.

name: Structural Surface Member Varying
definition: This entity describes surface members with varying section properties. The properties are provided by means of [[Pset_StructuralSurfaceMemberVaryingThickness]] via IfcRelDefinesByProperties,An instance of [[IfcStructuralSurfaceMemberVarying]] may be composed of two or more instances of [[IfcStructuralSurfaceMember]] with differing section properties. These subordinate members relate to the instance of [[IfcStructuralSurfaceMemberVarying]] by IfcRelAggregates.

name: Structural Surface Reaction
definition: This entity defines a reaction which occurs distributed over a surface. A surface reaction may be connected with a surface member or surface connection.

name: Bilinear
definition: The load value is bilinearly distributed over the load's extent.

name: Const
definition: The load has a constant value over its entire extent.

name: Discrete
definition: The load is specified as a series of discrete load points.

name: Isocontour
definition: The load is specified by a series of iso-curves (level sets), i.e. curves at which the load value is constant. These curves run perpendicularly to the load gradient.

name: Surface Feature
definition: A surface feature is a modification at (onto, or into) of the surface of an element. Parts of the surface of the entire surface may be affected. The volume and mass of the element may be increased, remain unchanged, or be decreased by the surface feature, depending on manufacturing technology. However, any increase or decrease of volume is small compared to the total volume of the element.

name: Defect
definition: Detected defect on the surface of an element, such as corroded or eroded area.

name: Hatch Marking
definition: surface markings defined by enclosed 2d shape with defined hatch fillings.

name: Line Marking
definition: 2D lines painted on pavement surfaces to form boundaries, centrelines and edge markings.

name: Mark
definition: A point, line, cross, or other mark, applied for example for easier adjustment of elements during assembly.

name: Nonskid Surfacing
definition: Paint or surfacing to prevent sliding or skidding.

name: Pavement Surface Marking
definition: Painted or chemical lines or symbols on the surface of pavements (a road or paved area)

name: Rumble Strip
definition: Raised and often textured strips on road center line or on shoulder, or across lanes to alert drivers by vibration and noise. Also Jiggle bars.

name: Symbol Marking
definition: Surface markings that convey information in the form of symbols and shapes such as arrows, text or pictorial symbols.

name: Tag
definition: A name tag, which allows to identify an element during production, delivery and assembly. May be manufactured in different ways, e.g. by printing or punching the tracking code onto the element or by attaching an actual tag.

name: Transverse Rumble Strip
definition: [[Type]] of rumble strip running across lane(s).

name: Treatment
definition: A subtractive surface feature, e.g. grinding, or an additive surface feature, e.g. coating, or an impregnating treatment, or a series of any of these kinds of treatments.

name: Switching Device
definition: A switch is used in a cable distribution system (electrical circuit) to control or modulate the flow of electricity.

name: Contact or
definition: An electrical device used to control the flow of power in a circuit on or off.

name: Dimmer Switch
definition: A dimmer switch has variable positions, and may adjust electrical power or other setting (according to the switched port type).

name: Emergency Stop
definition: An emergency stop device acts to remove as quickly as possible any danger that may have arisen unexpectedly.

name: Key Pad
definition: A set of buttons or switches, each potentially applicable to a different device.

name: Momentary Switch
definition: A momentary switch has no position, and may trigger some action to occur.

name: Relay
definition: A device designed to produce sudden predetermined changes in one or more electric output circuits, when certain conditions are fulfilled in the electric input circuits controlling the device.;definition from IEC 60050 151-13-31.

name: Selector Switch
definition: A selector switch has multiple positions, and may change the source or level of power or other setting (according to the switched port type).

name: Starter
definition: A starter is a switch which in the closed position controls the application of power to an electrical device.

name: Start and Stop Equipment
definition: A switch for alternatively closing and opening one or more electric circuits.

name: Switch Disconnector
definition: A switch disconnector is a switch which in the open position satisfies the isolating requirements specified for a disconnector.

name: Toggle Switch
definition: A toggle switch has two positions, and may enable or isolate electrical power or other setting (according to the switched port type).

name: System
definition: A system is an organized combination of related parts within an AEC product, composed for a common purpose or function or to provide a service. A system is essentially a functionally related aggregation of products. The grouping relationship to one or several instances of [[IfcProduct]] (the system members) is handled by IfcRelAssignsToGroup.

name: System Furniture Element
definition: A system furniture element defines components of modular furniture which are not directly placed in a building structure but aggregated inside furniture.

name: Panel
definition: Vertical panel used to divide work spaces.

name: Subrack
definition: A subrack is a part of technical cabinet which is used to store and mount pluggable electric subunits.

name: Work Surface
definition: Workstation countertop.

name: Tank
definition: A tank is a vessel or container in which a fluid or gas is stored for later use.

name: Basin
definition: An arbitrary open tank type.

name: Break Pressure
definition: An open container that breaks the hydraulic pressure in a distribution system, typically located between the fluid reservoir and the fluid supply points. A typical break pressure tank allows the flow to discharge into the atmosphere, thereby reducing its hydrostatic pressure to zero.

name: Expansion
definition: A closed container used in a closed fluid distribution system to mitigate the effects of thermal expansion or water hammer. The tank is typically constructed with a diaphragm dividing the tank into two sections, with fluid on one side of the diaphragm and air on the other. One example application is when connected to the primary circuit of a hot water system to accommodate the increase in volume of the water when it is heated.

name: Feed and Expansion
definition: An open tank that is used for both storage and thermal expansion. A typical example is a tank used to store make-up water at ambient pressure for supply to a hot water system, simultaneously accommodating increases in volume of the water when heated.

name: Oil Retention Tray
definition: An open container for environmental protection and storage of chemical products.

name: Pressure Vessel
definition: A closed container used for storing fluids or gases at a pressure different from the ambient pressure. A pressure vessel is typically rated by an authority having jurisdiction for the operational pressure.

name: Storage
definition: An open or closed container used for storing a fluid at ambient pressure and from which it can be supplied to the fluid distribution system. There are many examples of storage tanks, such as potable water storage tanks, fuel storage tanks, etc.

name: Vessel
definition: An arbitrary closed tank type.

name: Task
definition: An [[IfcTask]] is an identifiable unit of work to be carried out in a construction project.

name: Adjustment
definition: Making changes to the physical configuration of something.

name: Attendance
definition: Attendance or waiting on other things happening.

name: Calibration
definition: Making changes to the operational configuration of something.

name: Construction
definition: Constructing or building something.

name: Demolition
definition: Demolishing or breaking down something.

name: Dismantle
definition: Taking something apart carefully so that it can be recycled or reused.

name: Disposal
definition: Disposing or getting rid of something.

name: Emergency
definition: Tasks required when responding to, or ensuring the ability to respond to, an emergency situation.

name: Inspection
definition: Check if something is installed and is operating within expected parameters.

name: Installation
definition: Installing something (equivalent to construction but more commonly used for engineering tasks).

name: Logistic
definition: Transportation or delivery of something.

name: Maintenance
definition: Tasks required to keep an object in good working order.

name: Move
definition: Moving things from one place to another.

name: Operation
definition: A procedure undertaken to start up the operation an artifact.

name: Removal
definition: Removal of an item from use and taking it from its place of use.

name: Renovation
definition: Bringing something to an 'as-new' state.

name: Safety
definition: Tasks required to ensure safe use of the object. For example electrical 'lock-out' instructions.

name: Shutdown
definition: The set of tasks required for an orderly shut down without adverse impacts, typically applied to systems.

name: Startup
definition: The set of tasks required to begin or restart operation without adverse impacts, typically applied to systems.

name: Testing
definition: The set of tasks required to evaluate the performance of an object, to ensure if something is installed and is operating within expected parameters.

name: Troubleshooting
definition: The set of tasks required to diagnose commonly encountered performance problems, typically applied to element types and systems.

name: Tendon
definition: A tendon is a steel element such as a wire, cable, bar, rod, or strand used to impart prestress to concrete when the element is tensioned.

name: Tendon Anchor
definition: A tendon anchor is the end connection for tendons in prestressed or posttensioned concrete.

name: Coupler
definition: The anchor is an intermediate device which connects two tendons.

name: Fixed End
definition: The anchor fixes the end of a tendon.

name: Tensioning End
definition: The anchor is used or can be used to prestress the tendon.

name: Bar
definition: The tendon is configured as a bar.

name: Coated
definition: The tendon is coated.

name: Tendon Conduit
definition: A TendonConduit represents the components of the conduit system for tendons embedded in concrete structure.

name: Coupler
definition: A part to connect the conduits located in two different deck segments and related to the same tendon.

name: Diabolo
definition: A part of tendon conduit associated to deviator.

name: Duct
definition: A Sleeve or duct is related to the thickness of the conduit depending on the conduit, either cast into the concrete structure or placed adjacent to it.

name: Grouting Duct
definition: An additional small conduit connected to the main conduit to allow grouting in case of bonded post-tensioning, such as Grout inlet, Grout outlet and Grout vent.

name: Trumpet
definition: A specific part of conduit which has to be widened when reaching the tendon anchor because the strands are connected individually on the anchor.

name: Strand
definition: The tendon is a strand.

name: Wire
definition: The tendon is a wire.

name: Texture Coordinate Indices
definition: The [[IfcTextureCoordinateIndices]] provide the texture coordinates for an IfcIndexedPolygonalFace. The [[TexCoordIndex]] holds a list of indices pointing into the IfcTextureVertexList for texture coordinates that correspond to the TexCoordsOf.CoordIndex holding a list of indices pointing into the IfcCartesianPointList3D for vertex coordinates.

name: Texture Coordinate Indices with Voids
definition: The [[IfcTextureCoordinateIndicesWithVoids]] is a subtype of [[IfcTextureCoordinateIndices]] to be used to provide texture coordinates to polygonal faces with inner loops.

name: Track Element
definition: A track element is a built element used specifically in the track domain in railway.

name: Blocking Device
definition: A device composed of pneumatic, mechanic or electric components causing the braking of a train in case of emergency.

name: Derailer
definition: A fixed device which, when placed on the rail, derails the wheels of a vehicle, and serves to protect a converging line.;definition from IEC 60050-821.

name: Frog
definition: A frog is an arrangement ensuring the intersection of two opposite running edges of turnouts or diamond crossings and having one crossing vee and two wing rails.;definition from EN 13232-1-2004.

name: Half Set of Blades
definition: A half set of blades consists of one stock rail and its switch rail complete with small fittings. It is right or left hand as seen by an observer in the centre of the track facing the switch heel from the switch toe.;definition from EN 13232-1-2004.

name: Sleeper
definition: A sleeper is a track element that supports running rails, guard rails and check rails usually at right angles to its axis.

name: Speed Regulator
definition: A device composed of pneumatic, mechanic or electric components causing the breaking of a train in case of emergency.

name: Track End of Alignment
definition: A track end of alignment is a special functional installation such as axle-gauge changeover point or transporter wagon loading point.

name: Vehicle Stop
definition: A fixed installation at the end of the track which stops any vehicle movement (e.g., buffer stop, sand hump, etc.).

name: Transformer
definition: A transformer is an inductive stationary device that transfers electrical energy from one circuit to another.

name: Chopper
definition: A chopper is an electronic power DC convertor without an intermediate AC link giving a variable output voltage by varying the periods of conduction and non-conduction in an adjustable ratio.

name: Combined
definition: A transformer that changes different quantities between circuits.

name: Current
definition: A transformer that changes the current between circuits.

name: Frequency
definition: A transformer that changes the frequency between circuits.

name: Inverter
definition: A transformer that converts from direct current (DC) to alternating current (AC).

name: Rectifier
definition: A transformer that converts from alternating current (AC) to direct current (DC).

name: Voltage
definition: A transformer that changes the voltage between circuits.

name: Transport Element
definition: A transport element is a generalization of all transport related objects that move people, animals or goods within a Facility. The [[IfcTransportElement]] defines the occurrence of a transport element, that (if given), is expressed by the IfcTransportElementType.

name: Craneway
definition: A crane way system, normally including the crane rails, fasteners and the crane. It is primarily used to move heavy goods in a factory or other industry buildings.

name: Elevator
definition: Elevator or lift being a transport device to move people or goods vertically.

name: Escalator
definition: Escalator being a transport device to move people. It consists of individual linked steps that move up and down on tracks while keeping the threads horizontal.

name: Hauling Gear
definition: A device used for hauling goods.

name: Lifting Gear
definition: A device used for lifting or lowering heavy goods. It may be manually operated or electrically or pneumatically driven.

name: Moving Walkway
definition: Moving walkway being a transport device to move people horizontally or on an incline. It is a slow conveyor belt that transports people.

name: Transportation Device
definition: Abstract intermediate supertype for transportation devices.

name: Tube Bundle
definition: A tube bundle is a device consisting of tubes and bundles of tubes used for heat transfer and contained typically within other energy conversion devices, such as a chiller or coil.

name: Finned
definition: Finned tube bundle type.

name: Unitary Control Element
definition: A unitary control element combines a number of control components into a single product, such as a thermostat or humidistat.

name: Alarm Panel
definition: A control element at which alarms are annunciated.

name: Base Station Controller
definition: A base station controller (BSC) is a network component with the functions for controlling one or more base transceiver stations. BSC is responsible for the management of various interfaces, wireless resources and parameters, the signalling processing of call establishment and the channel allocation in the cell.

name: Combined
definition: Combination of at least two predefined types of unitary control element.

name: Control Panel
definition: A control element at which devices that control or monitor the operation of a site, building or part of a building are located

name: Gas Detection Panel
definition: A control element at which the detection of gas is annunciated.

name: Humidistat
definition: A control element that senses and regulates the humidity of a system or space so that the humidity is maintained near a desired setpoint.

name: Indicator Panel
definition: A control element at which equipment operational status, condition, safety state or other required parameters are indicated.

name: Mimic Panel
definition: A control element at which information that is available elsewhere is repeated or 'mimicked'.

name: Thermostat
definition: A control element that senses and regulates the temperature of an element, system or space so that the temperature is maintained near a desired setpoint.

name: Weather Station
definition: A control element that senses multiple climate properties such as temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, and rain.

name: Unitary Equipment
definition: Unitary equipment typically combine a number of components into a single product, such as air handlers, pre-packaged rooftop air-conditioning units, heat pumps, and split systems.

name: Air Conditioning Unit
definition: A unitary packaged air-conditioning unit typically used in residential or light commercial applications.

name: Air Handler
definition: A unitary air handling unit typically containing a fan, economizer, and coils.

name: Dehumidifier
definition: A unitary packaged dehumidification unit.units supporting multiple modes (dehumidification, cooling, and/or heating) should use AIRCONDITIONINGUNIT.

name: Roof Top Unit
definition: A packaged assembly that is either field-erected or manufactured atop the roof of a large residential or commercial building and acts as a unitary component.

name: Split System
definition: A system which separates the compressor from the evaporator, but acts as a unitary component typically within residential or light commercial applications.

name: Valve
definition: A valve is used in a building services piping distribution system to control or modulate the flow of the fluid.

name: Air Release
definition: Valve used to release air from a pipe or fitting.

name: Anti Vacuum
definition: Valve that opens to admit air if the pressure falls below atmospheric pressure.

name: Change Over
definition: Valve that enables flow to be switched between pipelines (3 or 4 port).

name: Check
definition: Valve that permits water to flow in one direction only and is enclosed when there is no flow (2 port).

name: Commissioning
definition: Valve used to facilitate commissioning of a system (2 port).

name: Diverting
definition: Valve that enables flow to be diverted from one branch of a pipeline to another (3 port).

name: Double Check
definition: An assembly that incorporates two valves used to prevent backflow.

name: Double Regulating
definition: Valve used to facilitate regulation of fluid flow in a system.

name: Draw Off Cock
definition: A valve used to remove fluid from a piping system.

name: Faucet
definition: Faucet valve typically used as a flow discharge.

name: Flushing
definition: Valve that flushes a predetermined quantity of water to cleanse a toilet, urinal, etc.

name: Gas Cock
definition: Valve that is used for controlling the flow of gas.

name: Gas Tap
definition: Gas tap typically used for venting or discharging gas from a system.

name: Isolating
definition: Valve that closes off flow in a pipeline.

name: Mixing
definition: Valve that enables flow from two branches of a pipeline to be mixed together (3 port).

name: Pressure Reducing
definition: Valve that reduces the pressure of a fluid immediately downstream of its position in a pipeline to a preselected value or by a predetermined ratio.

name: Pressure Relief
definition: Spring or weight loaded valve that automatically discharges to a safe place fluid that has built up to excessive pressure in pipes or fittings.

name: Regulating
definition: Valve used to facilitate regulation of fluid flow in a system.

name: Safety Cut Off
definition: Valve that closes under the action of a safety mechanism such as a drop weight, solenoid etc.

name: Steamtrap
definition: Valve that restricts flow of steam while allowing condensate to pass through.

name: Stop Cock
definition: An isolating valve used on a domestic water service.

name: Vehicle
definition: Piece of equipment designed to transport people or cargo.

name: Cargo
definition: A mobile transport element that represents a discrete unit of cargo managed by a facility.

name: Rolling Stock
definition: Refers to railway vehicles, including both powered and unpowered vehicles, for example locomotives, railroad cars, coaches, private railroad cars and wagons.

name: Vehicle
definition: A generalisation of a vehicle that interacts with a facility (e.g. as a user/customer) or as a specified operational asset within the facility.

name: Vehicle Air
definition: A specialisation of a vehicle that represents powered and unpowered flying vehicles, such as airplanes, helicopters, gliders etc.

name: Vehicle Marine
definition: A specialisation of a vehicle that operates on water as a marine vessel.

name: Vehicle Tracked
definition: A specialisation of a vehicle that operates on land tracked (Caterpillar).

name: Vehicle Wheeled
definition: A specialisation of a vehicle that operates on land as a multi wheeled vehicle such as a car, lorry, forklift etc.

name: Vibration Damper
definition: A vibration damper is a device used to minimize the effects of vibration in a structure by dissipating kinetic energy. The damper may be passive (elastic, frictional, inertia) or active (in a system using sensors and actuators).

name: Axial Yield
definition: A displacement dependent type damper in which the resistance force generated is determined by the plastic strain amount utilizing the plastic deformation of the steel material. The axial yield type is a damper that yields energy by absorbing the steel material against deformation in the axial direction, that is, in the direction of expansion and contraction.

name: Bending Yield
definition: A displacement dependent type damper in which the resistance force generated is determined by the plastic strain amount utilizing the plastic deformation of the steel material. The bending yield type is a damper, which yields steel material by bending.

name: Friction
definition: The friction type is a damper utilizing friction acting on the contact surface of a material.

name: Rubber
definition: The rubber mold is a damper that absorbs energy by utilizing deformation of laminated rubber. The difference between the seismic isolation bearing and the rubber type damper is whether or not to support the weight of the upper structures. The rubber damper does not transmit the weight of the upper structures to the sub structure.

name: Shear Yield
definition: A displacement dependent type damper in which the resistance force generated is determined by the plastic strain amount utilizing the plastic deformation of the steel material. The shear yield type is a damper, which causes the steel material to yield for deformation in the direction perpendicular to the member.

name: Viscous
definition: The viscous type is a damper that absorbs energy by utilizing the resistance of a viscous body.

name: Vibration Isolator
definition: A vibration isolator is a device used to minimize the effects of vibration transmissibility in a structure.

name: Base
definition: Base isolator preventing transfer of energy from the ground to the structure.

name: Compression
definition: Compression type vibration isolator.

name: Spring
definition: Spring type vibration isolator.

name: Virtual Element
definition: A virtual element is a special element used to provide imaginary, placeholder, or provisional areas, volumes, and boundaries. Virtual elements are usually not displayed and do not have quantities, associated materials, and other measures.

name: Boundary
definition: An imaginary boundary, such as between two adjacent spaces that are not separated by a physical boundary.

name: Clearance
definition: The virtual element denotes a clearance area or volume.

name: Provision for Void
definition: The virtual element denotes a proposed provision for voids (an proposed opening not applied as void yet).

name: Voiding Feature
definition: A voiding feature is a modification of an element which reduces its volume. Such a feature may be manufactured in different ways, for example by cutting, drilling, or milling of members made of various materials, or by inlays into the formwork of cast members made of materials such as concrete.

name: Chamfer
definition: A skewed plane end cut, removing material only across a part of the profile of the voided element.

name: Cutout
definition: An internal cutout (creating an opening) or external cutout (creating a recess) of arbitrary shape. The edges between cutting planes may be overcut or undercut, i.e. rounded.

name: Edge
definition: A shape modification along an edge of the element with the edge length as the predominant dimension of the feature, and feature profile dimensions which are typically much smaller than the edge length. Can for example be a chamfer edge (differentiated from a chamfer by its ratio of dimensions and thus usually manufactured differently), rounded edge (a convex edge feature), or fillet edge (a concave edge feature).

name: Hole
definition: A circular or slotted or threaded hole, typically but not necessarily of smaller dimension than what would be considered a cutout.

name: Miter
definition: A skewed plane end cut, removing material across the entire profile of the voided element.

name: Notch
definition: An external cutout of with a mostly rectangular cutting profile. The edges between cutting planes may be overcut or undercut, i.e. rounded.

name: Wall
definition: The wall represents a vertical construction that may bound or subdivide spaces. Wall are usually vertical, or nearly vertical, planar elements, often designed to bear structural loads. A wall is however not required to be load bearing.

name: Elemented Wall
definition: A stud wall framed with studs and faced with sheetings, sidings, wallboard, or plasterwork.

name: Movable
definition: A movable wall that is either movable, such as folding wall or a sliding wall, or can be easily removed as a removable partitioning or mounting wall. Movable walls do normally not define space boundaries and often belong to the furnishing system.

name: Parapet
definition: A wall-like barrier to protect human or vehicle from falling, or to prevent the spread of fires. Often designed at the edge of balconies, terraces or roofs, or along edges of bridges.

name: Partitioning
definition: A wall designed to partition spaces that often has a light-weight, sandwich-like construction (e.g. using gypsum board). Partitioning walls are normally non load bearing.

name: Plumbing Wall
definition: A pier, or enclosure, or encasement, normally used to enclose plumbing in sanitary rooms. Such walls often do not extend to the ceiling.

name: Polygonal
definition: A polygonal wall, extruded vertically, where the wall thickness varies along the wall path.

name: Retaining Wall
definition: A supporting wall used to protect against soil layers behind. Special types of a retaining wall may be e.g. Gabion wall and Grib wall. Examples of retaining walls are wing wall, headwall, stem wall, pierwall and protecting wall.

name: Shear
definition: A wall designed to withstand shear loads. Examples of shear wall are diaphragms inside a box girder, typically on a pier, to resist lateral forces and transfer them to the support.

name: Solid Wall
definition: A massive wall construction for the wall core being the single layer or having multiple layers attached. Such walls are often masonry or concrete walls (both cast in-situ or precast) that are load bearing and fire protecting.

name: Standard
definition: A standard wall, extruded vertically with a constant thickness along the wall path.;

name: Wave Wall
definition: Protective wall or screen to block overtopping and impact of waves across a breakwater

name: Waste Terminal
definition: A waste terminal has the purpose of collecting or intercepting waste from one or more sanitary terminals or other fluid waste generating equipment and discharging it into a single waste/drainage system.

name: Floortrap
definition: Pipe fitting, set into the floor, that retains liquid to prevent the passage of foul air

name: Floor Waste
definition: Pipe fitting, set into the floor, that collects waste water and discharges it to a separate trap.

name: Gully Sump
definition: Pipe fitting or assembly of fittings to receive surface water or waste water, fitted with a grating or sealed cover.

name: Gullytrap
definition: Pipe fitting or assembly of fittings that receives surface water or waste water; fitted with a grating or sealed cover that discharges water through a trap.

name: Roofd Rain
definition: Pipe fitting, set into the roof, that collects rainwater for discharge into the rainwater system.

name: Waste Disposal Unit
definition: Electrically operated device that reduces kitchen or other waste into fragments small enough to be flushed into a drainage system.

name: Waste Trap
definition: Pipe fitting, set adjacent to a sanitary terminal, that retains liquid to prevent the passage of foul air.

name: Window
definition: The window is a building element that is predominately used to provide natural light and fresh air. It includes vertical opening but also horizontal opening such as skylights or light domes. It includes constructions with swinging, pivoting, sliding, or revolving panels and fixed panels. A window consists of a lining and one or several panels.

name: Light Dome
definition: A special window that lies horizonally in a roof slab opening.

name: Sky Light
definition: A window within a sloped building element, usually a roof slab.

name: Window
definition: A standard window usually within a wall opening, as a window panel in a curtain wall, or as a 'free standing' window.

name: Work Calendar
definition: An [[IfcWorkCalendar]] defines working and non-working time periods for tasks and resources. It enables to define both specific time periods,00 on 25th August 2009, as well as repetitive time periods based on frequently used recurrence patterns,00 between 1st March 2009 and 31st December 2009.

name: First Shift
definition: Belongs to the first shift.

name: Second Shift
definition: Belongs to the second shift.

name: Third Shift
definition: Belongs to the third shift.

name: Work Control
definition: An [[IfcWorkControl]] is an abstract supertype which captures information that is common to both [[IfcWorkPlan]] and [[IfcWorkSchedule]].

name: Work Plan
definition: An [[IfcWorkPlan]] represents work plans in a construction or a facilities management project.

name: Actual
definition: A control in which actual items undertaken are indicated.

name: Baseline
definition: A control that is a baseline from which changes that are made later can be recognized.

name: Planned
definition: Planned

name: Work Schedule
definition: An [[IfcWorkSchedule]] represents a task schedule of a work plan, which in turn can contain a set of schedules for different purposes.

name: Actual
definition: A process in which actual items undertaken are indicated.

name: Baseline
definition: A process that is a baseline from which changes that are made later can be recognized.

name: Planned
definition: A process showing planned items.

name: Zone
definition: A zone is a group of spaces, partial spaces or other zones. These spaces may or may not be adjacent. A zone does not have its own shape representation. Zone structures may not be hierarchical (in contrary to the spatial structure of a project - see [[IfcSpatialStructureElement]]), i.e. one individual [[IfcSpace]] may be associated with zero, one, or several [[IfcZone]]'s. [[IfcSpace]]'s are grouped into an [[IfcZone]] by using the objectified relationship IfcRelAssignsToGroup as specified at the supertype [[IfcGroup]]. For example, a zone might be used to represent an apartment as a group of spaces.
